articles.title: इनड्राइभ नेपालद्वारा ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ प्रमाणपत्र प्रदान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं, नेपाल । विश्वव्यापी मोबिलिटी तथा डेलिभरी प्लेटफर्म इनड्राइभले महिलालाई ड्राइभिङ पेसामा अघि बढ्न समान अवसर सिर्जना गर्ने उद्देश्यले सञ्चालन गरेको ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ कार्यक्रमको पहिलो चरण सफलतापूर्वक सम्पन्न गरेको छ ।

कार्यक्रमअन्तर्गत काठमाडौंमा आयोजित प्रमाणपत्र वितरण समारोहमा तीन महिनाको प्रशिक्षण पूरा गरेका १० जना महिलालाई सम्मान गरिएको छ । सुरक्षित र आत्मनिर्भर रूपमा दुईपाङ्ग्रे सवारी चलाउने पेसामा अघि बढ्न आवश्यक सीप, आत्मविश्वास र स्रोतसाधन प्रदान गर्ने उद्देश्यले सहभागीहरूलाई विभिन्न चरणमा प्रशिक्षण दिइएको थियो ।

अप्रिल २०२६ मा सुरु भएको ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ कार्यक्रम विशेषगरी अवसरबाट वञ्चित समुदायका महिलालाई मोबिलिटी क्षेत्रमा आर्थिक अवसरमा पहुँच दिलाउने उद्देश्यले सञ्चालन गरिएको हो । महिलालाई परम्परागत रूपमा पुरुषको वर्चस्व रहेको पेसामा प्रवेश गर्न बाधा पु¥याउने सामाजिक तथा व्यावहारिक अवरोधलाई कम गर्न पनि कार्यक्रमले जोड दिएको छ ।

प्रशिक्षण अवधिभर सडक सुरक्षालाई व्यावसायिक दक्षताको महत्वपूर्ण पक्षका रूपमा समेटिएको थियो । सहभागीहरूलाई व्यावहारिक राइडिङ प्रशिक्षणसँगै सडक सुरक्षासम्बन्धी मार्गदर्शन प्रदान गर्नुका साथै औपचारिक सवारी चालक अनुमतिपत्र (लाइसेन्स) प्राप्त गर्ने प्रक्रियामा समेत सहयोग गरिएको थियो ।

प्रत्येक सहभागीलाई सुरक्षात्मक हेल्मेट तथा प्राथमिक उपचार र स्वास्थ्यसम्बन्धी सामग्रीसहितको सुरक्षा किट प्रदान गरिएको थियो ।

व्यक्तिगत सुरक्षालाई पनि प्रशिक्षणको छुट्टै महत्वपूर्ण पक्षका रूपमा समेटिएको थियो । फाइटब्याक नेपाल सँगको सहकार्यमा उन्नत आत्मरक्षा तालिम सञ्चालन गरिएको थियो, जसले सहभागीहरूलाई सम्भावित सुरक्षा चुनौती पहिचान गर्न, आत्मविश्वास बढाउन र आवश्यक अवस्थामा व्यवहारिक रूपमा सामना गर्न सक्ने सीप विकास गर्न सहयोग गरेको थियो ।

काठमाडौं उपत्यका ट्राफिक प्रहरी कार्यालयका डीएसपी सुनिलजंग शाहले भने, “सडक सुरक्षा सबैको साझा जिम्मेवारी हो र यसमा प्रत्येक चालकको महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका हुन्छ । हामी सहभागीहरूलाई ट्राफिक नियमको पालना गर्न, सडकमा सधैं सचेत रहन र अनुभव बढाउँदै निरन्तर सिकिरहन आग्रह गर्छौं । सबै सहभागीलाई बधाई दिँदै व्यावसायिक चालकका रूपमा उनीहरूको सुरक्षित र सफल यात्राका लागि शुभकामना व्यक्त गर्दछौं ।”

मोबिलिटीमा महिलाको पहुँच विस्तार यस समूहका महिलाका लागि सवारी चालक अनुमतिपत्र केवल आम्दानीको माध्यम मात्र नभई आफ्नो काम, शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य सेवा तथा बजारसम्म आफ्नै समयअनुसार स्वतन्त्र रूपमा पुग्ने अवसर पनि हो । यसले सार्वजनिक यातायातको समयतालिका वा परिवारका अन्य सदस्यमा निर्भर रहनुपर्ने अवस्थालाई कम गर्न सहयोग पु¥याउँछ ।

दुईपाङ्ग्रे सवारीमा आधारित राइड–हेलिङ सेवाले चारपाङ्ग्रे सवारी पुग्न कठिन हुने साँघुरा गल्ली तथा अन्तिम गन्तव्यसम्म पनि सेवा पु¥याउन सक्छ । सामान्यतया यसको भाडा पनि चारपाङ्ग्रे सवारीको तुलनामा कम हुने गर्दछ । राइड–हेलिङ सेवामा महिलाको सहभागिता बढ्दा यात्रुहरूले आफूलाई उपयुक्त चालक छनोट गर्ने थप अवसरसमेत पाउनेछन् ।

प्रमाणपत्र वितरण समारोह प्रमाणपत्र वितरण समारोहमा साझेदार संस्थाका प्रतिनिधि, सरकारी निकायका सरोकारवाला, सञ्चारकर्मी तथा विशिष्ट अतिथिहरूको सहभागिता रहेको थियो ।

समारोहमा इनड्राइभका प्रतिनिधि तथा इनड्राइभ नेपालकी ब्रान्ड एम्बेसडर स्वस्तिमा खड्काले कार्यक्रम सफलतापूर्वक सम्पन्न गरेका १० जना सहभागीलाई प्रमाणपत्र, सुरक्षा किट तथा मायाको चिनो प्रदान गरे । कार्यक्रममा सहभागी १० जना महिलाको ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ यात्रालाई समेटिएको भिडियोसमेत प्रदर्शन गरिएको थियो ।

समारोहका क्रममा सहभागीमध्ये एक जनालाई विद्युतीय स्कुटर, तीन जनालाई स्मार्टफोन र छ जनालाई स्मार्टवाच प्रदान गरिएको थियो । यी सामग्रीले उनीहरूलाई व्यावसायिक ड्राइभिङ यात्राको सुरुवातमा थप सहयोग पुग्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ ।

इनड्राइभ साउथ एसियाकि कम्युनिकेसन म्यनाजर शेरिन एर्विना कौरले भनिन्, “हामीले विभिन्न बजारमा एउटै अवस्था देखिरहेका छौं, राइड माग्ने यात्रुमध्ये धेरै महिला छन्, तर उनीहरूलाई राइड दिने चालकमा महिलाको संख्या निकै कम छ । यो महिलाले यस्तो काम गर्न चाहन्छन् कि चाहँदैनन् भन्ने विषय थिएन। मुख्य प्रश्न उनीहरूका लागि यो पेसामा प्रवेश गर्ने बाटो उपलब्ध थियो कि थिएन भन्ने थियो । नेपालमा सञ्चालन गरिएको पहिलो समूहले तालिम, लाइसेन्स र प्लेटफर्ममा पहुँचलाई एउटै यात्राका रूपमा जोड्दा कस्तो परिवर्तन सम्भव हुन्छ भन्ने देखाएको छ। हामी अन्य बजारमा पनि यसबाट सिक्दै कार्यक्रमलाई अघि बढाउनेछौं ।”

इनड्राइभ नेपालकी कम्युनिकेसन्स म्यानेजर मञ्जिता गुरुङले भनिन्, “सीप विकास तालिम यस यात्राको एउटा हिस्सा मात्र हो । सामाजिक सोच र धारणाले पनि उत्तिकै महत्व राख्छ, र महिलाले ड्राइभिङ सुरु गरेपछि उनी प्रवेश गर्ने वातावरण पनि महत्वपूर्ण हुन्छ । ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ महिलालाई लाइसेन्स प्राप्त गर्नेदेखि आत्मविश्वास विकास गर्ने, परिवारमा यसबारे संवाद गर्ने र आम्दानीको अवसर सिर्जना गर्नेसम्म हरेक पक्षमा सहयोग गर्ने गरी तयार गरिएको हो । जब धेरै महिलाहरू यो पेसामा आउँछन्, यात्रुहरूले पनि लाभ पाउँछन्, उनीहरूसँग आफूलाई राइड गराउने चालक छनोट गर्ने थप विकल्प हुन्छ ।”

इनड्राइभ नेपालकी सिनियर ड्राइभर अपरेसन्स स्पेसलिस्ट सुनिता जीमी राईले भनिन्, “इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ महिलाका लागि थप सहयोगी वातावरण निर्माण गर्ने दिशामा महत्वपूर्ण कदम हो । जब धेरै महिलाहरूले सवारीको स्टेयरिङ समाउँछन्, उनीहरूले नेपाललाई थप समावेशी भविष्यतर्फ अघि बढाउन पनि भूमिका खेलिरहेका हुन्छन् ।”

इनड्राइभ नेपालकी ब्रान्ड एम्बेसडर स्वस्तिमा खड्काले भनिन्, “‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ ले अन्यायलाई चुनौती दिँदै समुदायमा सकारात्मक परिवर्तन ल्याउने इनड्राइभको प्रतिबद्धतालाई प्रतिबिम्बित गर्छ । मानिस र समानतालाई केन्द्रमा राखेर अघि बढाइएको यस पहलको हिस्सा बन्न पाउँदा म गर्व गर्छु ।”

articles.title: पार्टी निर्माणमा सि जिनपिङको अवधारणाबारे नेपालमा चर्चा
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालसहित विश्वमा राजनीतिक दलको निर्माण र त्यसको प्रभावकारी संचालनका लागि चिनियाँ राष्ट्रपति सि जिनपिङको अवधारणा उपयोगी हुने विज्ञहरुले बताएका छन् । फ्रेन्डस अन क्लाउडले काठमाडौंमा गरेको कार्यक्रममा राजनीतिज्ञ जगन्नाथ खतिवडा, परराष्ट्रविद डा गोपाल खनाल, पूर्व राजदूत महेशराज दाहाल, अनुसन्धानकर्ता डा। दीपक देवकोटा र क्लाउडका अध्यक्ष शोभित उप्रेतीले पार्टी निर्माणमा राष्ट्रपति सी का विभिन्न आयामबारे धारणा राखेका हुन् ।

कार्यक्रममा बो्ल्दै पूर्व राजदूत दाहालले राष्ट्रपति सिको अध्ययनशिल बानी नै पार्टी र राष्ट्र निर्माणका लागि आधारशिला बनेको उल्ले गरे ।

दाहालका अनुसार श्रम शिविरमा हुँदा पनि निकै अध्धयन गर्ने सी लामो र नयाँ सोचका थिए । सृजनशीलता परिवर्तनकारी सोचका धनी सीले पार्टी सदसयता पाउन पनि निकै संघर्ष गरेकाले पार्टी कस्तो हुनुपर्छ भन्ने पनि उनले राम्रोसँग बुझेका थिए ।

राम्रो दृष्टिकोण भए पार्टी र देश बन्छ भन्ने कुरा उनले प्रमाणित गरेर देखाए । भ्रष्टाचार विरुद्वका कार्यक्रम र दल भित्रको शुद्वतामा उनको जोड थियो । नेतृत्वको जिम्मेवारी र कर्तव्य । प्रविधि विकास, जनताको सहभागीता, विज्ञानमा लगानी उनको पार्टी निर्माणका प्रमुख साधन हुन ।

यस्तै , डा दिपक देवकोटाले राष्ट्रपति सीले राज्यबाट डर नभई भरोसा जगाउने काम गरेर सफलता प्राप्त गरेको धारणा राखे । जनतालाई केन्द्रमा राखेर पार्टी र देश निर्माण गर्न उनी सफल भए ।

जनताले विश्वास गर्ने पार्टी बनाउन राष्ट्रपति सी ले सुशासन र सुरक्षालाई प्राथमिकता दिएको उनले बताए । परराष्ट्र विद डा गोपाल खनालले विश्वव्यापी सुशासन अभियान र नयाँ युगका लागि चिनियाँ विशेषतासहितको समाजवाद नै सि जिनपिङको पार्टी निर्माणको स्पष्ट अवधारणा भएको बताए ।

पार्टी नियम र देश कानुनबाट चल्छ भन्ने कुरा राष्ट्रपति सी ले स्थापित गरेको उनको भनाइ छ । जनतालाई विकास दिने सोच नै सिको सोच भएको खनालको निष्कर्ष छ।

आर्थिक अनियमितता गर्ने ७० लाख भन्दा बढीलाई चीनमा कारबाही गरिएको जानकारी दिंदै खनालले राष्ट्रपति सी को सुशासन अभियानको प्रशंसा गरे ।

नेता जगन्नाथ खतिवडाले अनुशासन, अनुगमन र आत्मसमीक्षाको सुत्र न‌ै राष्ट्रपति सि को पार्टी र देश निर्माणको आधारशिला रहेको धारणा राखे ।

राष्ट्रपति सि ले विचार निर्माण, राजनीति निर्माण र संगठन निर्माणमा जोड दिंदै पार्टीमा गुणस्तरीय सदस्यलाई मात्र स्थान दिएको खतिवडाले बताए । चीन जस्तो शक्तिशाली राष्ट्र हाम्रो छिमेकी भएकाले दलीय एकता तथा दीर्घकालीन सोच र योजनाका साथ अघि बढ्ने कुरा नेपालले सिक्नुपर्ने खतिवडा बताउँछन् ।

articles.title: ग्लोबल आइएमई बैंकमा नागरिक एपबाटै खाता खोल्न सकिने
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । ग्लोबल आइएमई बैंक लिमिटेडले नागरिक एपसँगको सहकार्यमा नागरिक एपमार्फतै बैंक खाता खोल्न सकिने नयाँ सुविधा सुरु गरेको छ ।

राष्ट्रिय परिचयपत्रका आधारमा नागरिक एपमा आबद्ध नेपाली नागरिकले बैंकको वेबसाइटमा उपलब्ध क्यूआर कोड स्क्यान गरी व्यक्तिगत बचत खाता अनलाइनबाटै खोल्न सक्नेछन् ।

यो सेवा १८ वर्ष वा सोभन्दा माथिका राष्ट्रिय परिचयपत्र भएका तथा नागरिक एपमा आबद्ध व्यक्तिका लागि उपलब्ध हुनेछ । खाता खोल्ने क्रममा बैंकले ग्राहकको पूर्वसहमतिमा आवश्यक व्यक्तिगत विवरण नागरिक एपबाट सुरक्षित रूपमा प्राप्त गर्ने भएकाले पुनः विवरण भर्नुपर्ने झन्झट हट्ने, गोपनीयता कायम रहने र सूचनाको सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित हुने बैंकले जनाएको छ ।

नागरिक एपमार्फत खोलिएको खाता सञ्चालनका लागि भने ग्राहकले नजिकको शाखामा गई वा भिडियो केवाईसीमार्फत प्रमाणीकरण गर्नुपर्नेछ ।

बैंकका अनुसार सरकारी डिजिटल पूर्वाधारको उपयोग गर्दै सुरु गरिएको यो सेवाले खाता खोल्ने प्रक्रियालाई थप सहज, सुरक्षित, पारदर्शी र प्रविधिमैत्री बनाउनेछ । ग्राहकलाई आधुनिक डिजिटल बैंकिङ अनुभव प्रदान गर्ने विश्वास बैंकको छ ।

ग्लोबल आइएमई बैंक ७७ वटै जिल्लामा शाखा सञ्जाल विस्तार गर्ने निजी क्षेत्रको पहिलो वाणिज्य बैंक हो ।

हाल बैंकले ३४२ शाखा, ३६८ एटिएम, १४७ शाखारहित बैंकिङ सेवा, ६९ एक्सटेन्सन तथा राजस्व सङ्कलन काउन्टर र ३ वटा वैदेशिक प्रतिनिधि कार्यालयसहित १ हजारभन्दा बढी सेवा केन्द्रमार्फत सेवा दिँदै आएको छ ।

articles.title: मेलम्चीमा स्थानीय उत्पादन प्रवर्द्धनका लागि ‘कोशेली घर’ उद्घाटन
articles.summary:
मेलम्ची । स्थानीय कृषि र हस्तकला उत्पादनलाई प्रवर्द्धन गर्ने उद्देश्यले सिन्धुपाल्चोकको मेलम्ची बजारमा नयाँ व्यावसायिक केन्द्र “कोशेली घर” सञ्चालनमा आएको छ। साउन ८ देखि हरेक दिन बिहान ७ बजेदेखि राति ७ बजेसम्म खुल्ने यो कोशेलीघरको उद्घाटन नगरप्रमुख आइतमान तामाङले गरेका छन् ।

नगरप्रमुख तामाङले कोशेलीघरबाट ताजा फलफूल तथा तरकारी, घरेलु अचार, मह, भान्साका आवश्यक परिकार, हस्तकला सामग्री, अण्डा, माछा, गेडागुडी, चिया, कफी तथा हर्बल सामग्रीलगायत स्थानीय रैथाने उत्पादनको सीधा बिक्री वितरणमा जोड दिने बताए । उनले यहाँ राखिने विशेष परिकार तथा उत्पादनहरू आवश्यक परेमा जिल्ला बाहिर पनि पठाइने समेत जनाए ।

कोशेलीघरले स्थानीय उत्पादक र उपभोक्तालाई एउटै छानामुनि प्रत्यक्ष भेटघाटको व्यवस्था गराउँदै बजारसम्म पहुँच सहज बनाउने लक्ष्य लिएको प्रमुख तामाङले बताए ।

साथै प्रमुख प्रशासकीय अधिकृत निमेष मिश्रले ‘फार्म देखि किचनसम्म अवधारणाअनुरूप उत्पादक र उपभोक्ताको मागअनुसार नयाँ वस्तु तथा उत्पादनहरू परिष्कृत गरी सार्वजनिक गरिने र उद्यमीहरूको भेटघाट हुने उपयुक्त स्थलको रूपमा यसलाई विकास गर्ने योजना रहेको बताए । प्रारम्भिक अनुमान अनुसार नगरपालिकाले दैनिक हजारौंले यहाँबाट किनमेल गर्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

मेलम्ची आसपासका सरकारी तथा निजी कार्यालयका कर्मचारी, घुम्न आउने पर्यटक, स्थानीय टोल तथा छिमेकी पालिकाका बासिन्दाहरू प्रमुख लक्षित ग्राहक रहने कोशेलीघरबाट स्थानिय रोजगारी र व्यवसायिक गतिविधिलाई थप सक्रिय बनाउन मद्दत पुग्ने उपस्थित उपभोक्ताले विश्वास व्यक्त गरिएको थियो ।

articles.title: २४ औं अनसन शुरु, समर्थनसँगै विरोध पनि बढ्दै
articles.summary:
कैलाली । धनगढीस्थित कृष्ण मन्दिर धर्मशालामा डा. गोविन्द केसीको सत्याग्रह दोस्रो दिन पनि जारी छ । स्वास्थ्य क्षेत्र सुधारका पाँचबुँदे माग अघि सार्दै उनले शहीद दशरथचन्द स्वास्थ्य विज्ञान विश्वविद्यालय र चिकित्सा शिक्षा आयोगमा स्वार्थ बाझिने नियुक्ति खारेज गर्न, चिकित्सा शिक्षा ऐन संशोधन गर्न, छात्रवृत्ति कटौतीको निर्णय फिर्ता लिन र मापदण्ड नपुगेका निजी मेडिकल कलेजमा थप सिट स्वीकृति रोक्न सरकारसँग माग गरेका छन् ।

विगतका सहमति कार्यान्वयन, चिकित्सा शिक्षालाई गैरनाफामूलक बनाउने तथा भ्रष्टाचार र अपराधका आरोपमाथि निष्पक्ष अनुसन्धानको मागसमेत डा. केसीले गरेका छन् । डा. केसीले आफू विश्वविद्यालयको विरोधमा नभई स्वार्थ बाँझिने नियुक्तिको विरोधमा सत्याग्रहमा बसेको स्पष्ट पारेका छन् ।

यता शहीद दशरथचन्द स्वास्थ्य विज्ञान विश्वविद्यालय संघर्ष समितिले भने डा. केसीलाई सत्याग्रह स्थगित गर्न आग्रह गरेको छ ।

संयोजक लोकराज पाण्डेको नेतृत्वमा प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारीलाई भेटेको टोलीले आन्दोलनका कारण विश्वविद्यालय सञ्चालन र विकासको प्रक्रिया प्रभावित हुन सक्ने भन्दै आवश्यक पहल गर्न अनुरोध गरेको हो ।

उता, कृष्ण मन्दिर धर्मशाला व्यवस्थापन समितिले पूर्वसूचना बिना अनिश्चितकालीन सत्याग्रह सुरु गरिएको भन्दै डा. केसीलाई स्थान खाली गर्न पत्र दिएको छ । तर डा. केसीले व्यवस्थापन समितिसँग सहमतिमै सत्याग्रह सुरु गरेको दाबी गर्दै केही स्वार्थ समूहले आन्दोलन कमजोर पार्ने प्रयास गरिरहेको आरोप लगाए ।

उनले दबाब र अवरोधका बाबजुद आफ्ना मागबाट पछि नहट्ने र आवश्यक परे फुटपाथमै बसेर पनि सत्याग्रहलाई निरन्तरता दिने बताएका छन् ।

चिकित्सा शिक्षा सुधारको मागसँगै डा. केसीको आन्दोलन जारी रहँदा विश्वविद्यालय सञ्चालनमा असर पर्ने चिन्ता भने स्थानीय स्तरमा बढ्दै गएको छ ।

articles.title: २ लाख ऋण, १४ लाख तिर्दापनि जग्गा बैंकको कब्जामा !
articles.summary:
सप्तरी । सप्तरीको विष्णुपुर–६ मा माय जलपा बचत तथा ऋण सहकारीका अध्यक्षले ऋणीहरूको धितो जग्गा फिर्ता नगरी आफ्नै परिवारको नाममा नामसारी गरेर बैंकमा धितो राखेको आरोप लागेको छ । बैंकले लिलामी सूचना प्रकाशित गरेपछि पीडितहरू ठगीको तथ्य थाहा पाएसँगै जग्गा फिर्ता र दोषीमाथि कारबाहीको माग गर्दै न्यायको खोजीमा भौतारीरहेका छन् ।

सप्तरीको विष्णुपुर गाउँपालिका–६ रञ्जितपुरकी रेणु देवी दासले २०७२ सालमा माय जलपा बचत तथा ऋण सहकारी संस्था लिमिटेडबाट छोरीको विवाहका लागि दुई लाख रुपैयाँ ऋण लिएकी थिइन् । उनले ब्याजसहित पटक–पटक गरेर करिब १४ लाख रुपैयाँ तिरेर तीन वर्षअघि नै ऋण चुक्ता गरिन् । तर सहकारीका अध्यक्ष दिलिप यादवले घरको लालपुर्जा फिर्ता दिन आलटाल गर्दै आएका छन् ।

अहिले मल्टीपर्पस् फाइनान्स बैंकले उक्त घरजग्गा लिलामीको सूचना प्रकाशित गरेपछि सहकारी अध्यक्षको कर्तुत सार्वजनिक भएको छ भने पीडित परिवार न्यायको खोजीमा भौतारिएको छ । अनुसन्धानका क्रममा सहकारीका अध्यक्ष यादवले जग्गा आफ्नो पत्नी सुनिता यादवको नाममा नामसारी गराई सोही जग्गा धितो राखेर बैंकबाट ऋण लिएको आरोप लागेको छ । बैंकले लिलामी सूचना जारी गरेपछि मात्रै पीडितले आफ्नो जग्गा अर्कैको नाममा रहेको थाहा पाएका हुन् ।

लिलामी सूचना देखेपछि रेणु दास बैंक पुगेर आफ्नो जग्गाबारे जानकारी मागेकी थिइन् । बैंकले ऋण बराबरको रकम तिरेपछि मात्रै जग्गा फिर्ता गर्न सकिने जनाएको उनको भनाइ छ । त्यसपछि उनले सहकारी अध्यक्षलाई बैंक जान आग्रह गरे पनि उनले अस्वीकार गर्दै सम्पर्कबाट टाढिएका छन् ।

यस्तै स्थानीय पुलकित मुखियाले पनि ५० हजार रुपैयाँ ऋण लिएर धितो राखेको एक कठ्ठा जग्गा ऋण चुक्ता गर्दा समेत फिर्ता नपाएको र आफ्नो नामबाटै नामसारी गरिएको आरोप लगाएका छन् ।

पीडितहरू सहकारीका सञ्चालकले सम्पत्ति बेचेर फरार हुने आशंकामा छन् । उनीहरू आफ्नो जग्गा फिर्ता गराइ दोषीमाथि कारबाही गर्न सम्बन्धित निकायसँग न्यायको माग गरिरहेका छन् ।

articles.title: उजाड पाखामा चिया खेती, गाउँमै रोजगारी
articles.summary:
दोलखा । दोलखाको कालिञ्चोक गाउँपालिका–४ सुन्द्रावतीमा व्यावसायिक चिया खेतीले गाउँमै रोजगारी सिर्जना गरेको छ । बाँझो जमिन हरियो चिया बगानमा रूपान्तरण भएपछि महिला, ज्येष्ठ नागरिक र युवाले दैनिक १८ सय रुपैयाँसम्म आम्दानी गर्दै स्थानीय आर्थिक गतिविधिमा उल्लेख्य टेवा पु¥याएका छन् ।

दोलखाको कालिञ्चोक गाउँपालिका–९ सुन्द्रावतीमा व्यावसायिक चिया खेतीले गाउँको स्वरूप फेरिएको छ । रोजगारीको अभावका कारण हुने युवा पलायन र बाँदर आतंकजस्ता समस्याको समाधान गर्दै चिया खेती स्थानीयका लागि आयआर्जनको भरपर्दो माध्यम बनेको छ ।

पहिले उत्तिसको घारीले ढाकिएको र झुसुले किराको समस्याले विद्यालयका विद्यार्थीसमेत प्रभावित थिए । तर यो क्षेत्र वडा कार्यालयको पहलमा सफा गरी इलामबाट ल्याइएका २५ हजार चियाका बिरुवासहित हरियो चिया बगानमा रूपान्तरण गरिएको छ ।

प्रारम्भिक परीक्षण सफल भएपछि यसको व्यवस्थापनको जिम्मा स्थानीयको सहभागितामा बनेको सुन्द्रावती चिया विकास समूहलाई हस्तान्तरण गरिएको छ । ७–८ वर्षको अन्तरालमा यहाँ उत्पादित चियाले बजार पाउन थालेको छ ।

प्रति किलो १०० रुपैयाँका दरले चियाको मुना टिप्ने व्यवस्था भएपछि महिला, ज्येष्ठ नागरिक र परीक्षा दिएर बसेका विद्यार्थीले गाउँमै रोजगारी पाएका छन् । बिहानदेखि साँझसम्म काम गर्ने मजदुरले दैनिक १८ सय रुपैयाँसम्म आम्दानी गरिरहेका छन् ।

वडा कार्यालयको बजेट र लगानीमा अघि बढाइएको यस योजनामा चालु आर्थिक वर्ष मात्रै ४ लाख रुपैयाँ थप लगानी गरिएको छ । चिया प्रशोधन सहज बनाउन ६ लाख रुपैयाँ लागतमा तीन प्रकारका आधुनिक प्रशोधन मेसिनसमेत सञ्चालनमा ल्याइएको छ ।

स्थानीय सरकारको सही योजना र निरन्तर लगानी भए बाँझो जमिनलाई पनि आम्दानीको स्रोत बनाउन सकिने उदाहरण सुन्द्रावतीको चिया खेतीले प्रस्तुत गरेको छ ।

articles.title: मारुती सिमेन्टद्वारा जयन्ती मेमोरियल ट्रस्टलाई CPR तालिमका लागि म्यानिकिन हस्तान्तरण
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । हालको परिवेशमा विशेषगरी युवापुस्तामा अस्वस्थ जीवनशैली, अत्यधिक तनाव तथा हृदयसम्बन्धी आकस्मिक समस्याका घटनामा वृद्धि हुँदै गएको अवस्थालाई मध्यनजर गर्दै CPR (Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation) तालिमको आवश्यकता बढ्दै गएको छ।

यही आवश्यकतालाई महसुस गर्दै मारुती सिमेन्ट लिमिटेड ले आफ्नो सामाजिक उत्तरदायित्व (CSR) अन्तर्गत देशभर CPR तालिम सञ्चालन गर्ने उद्देश्यका साथ जयन्ती मेमोरियल ट्रस्ट लाई आवश्यक CPR Training Manikin हस्तान्तरण गरेको छ।

उक्त सामग्री हस्तान्तरण कार्यक्रम दुवै संस्थाका सञ्चालक तथा पदाधिकारीहरूको उपस्थितिमा सम्पन्न भएको हो। कार्यक्रममा मारुती सिमेन्ट लिमिटेडले समाजप्रतिको आफ्नो उत्तरदायित्व निर्वाह गर्ने प्रतिबद्धतालाई व्यवहारमा उतार्दै स्वास्थ्य सचेतना अभिवृद्धिमा सहयोग पुर्‍याउन पाउँदा खुशी लागेको जनाएको छ।

जयन्ती मेमोरियल ट्रस्टले प्राप्त CPR Training Manikin को प्रयोग गरी देशभर निःशुल्क वा पहुँचयोग्य CPR तालिम सञ्चालन गर्ने, आकस्मिक हृदयाघात वा अन्य आपत्कालीन अवस्थामा सर्वसाधारणले समयमै प्राथमिक उपचार प्रदान गर्न सक्ने जनशक्ति तयार गर्ने लक्ष्य रहेको जनाएको छ।

ट्रस्टका अनुसार CPR सम्बन्धी ज्ञान र सीपको विस्तारले आकस्मिक अवस्थामा बहुमूल्य जीवन बचाउन महत्वपूर्ण योगदान पुग्ने विश्वास गरिएको छ। यस सहकार्यले समुदायमा स्वास्थ्य सचेतना बढाउनुका साथै जीवनरक्षा सम्बन्धी सीप विकासमा महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका खेल्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

articles.title: सैनिक कल्याणकारी भवन ठेक्का प्रकरण : निर्माण व्यवसायीमाथि चरम अन्याय र अर्बौँको लगानी जोखिममा !
articles.summary:
काठमाडौँ । काठमाडौँको न्यूरोड महाँकालस्थानस्थित सैनिक कल्याणकारी कोषको स्वामित्वमा रहेको व्यावसायिक भवन भाडामा लिई अर्बौँ रुपैयाँ लगानी गरेको श्रीजयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रा. लि. चरम प्रशासनिक थिचोमिचो र अन्यायमा परेको निश्कर्ष निकालिएको छ ।

भवन हस्तान्तरणमा सेनाकै तर्फबाट भएको ढिलाइ, काठमाडौँ महानगरपालिकासँगको नक्सा पास विवाद र कोभिड–१९ को महामारीका कारण उत्पन्न विषम परिस्थितिलाई नजरअन्दाज गर्दै कल्याणकारी निर्देशनालयले उल्टै निर्माण व्यवसायीमाथि एकतर्फी रूपमा करोडौँ बक्यौताको भार थोपरेको पाइएको हो । यस विषयमा अहिले सर्वोच्च अदालतमा मुद्धा पुगेको छ । साथै यस विषयमा मानव अधिकार आयोगमा पनि उजुरी परेको छ ।

प्राप्त दस्तावेज तथा पत्राचारका अनुसार सैनिक कल्याणकारी कोष र श्रीजयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रा. लि. बीच २०७६ माघ १६ गते महाँकालस्थानस्थित ‘कल्याणकारी भवन’१५ वर्षका लागि भाडामा लिने सम्झौता भएको थियो । सम्झौताको मुख्य सर्त नै भवन विधिवत रूपमा पूर्ण निर्माण भई हस्तान्तरण भएपछि मात्र भाडा लागू हुने भन्ने थियो । तर, बोलपत्र जारी गर्दाकै बखत उक्त भवनको नक्सा पास नभएको र मापदण्ड विपरीत बढी निर्माण गरिएको भन्दै काठमाडौँ महानगरपालिकाले काम रोकेपछि सम्झौताको प्रारम्भिक चरणमै विवाद उत्पन्न भएको थियो । सैनिक कल्याणकारी निर्देशनालयको आफ्नै आन्तरिक र कानुनी त्रुटिका कारण समयमा भवन हस्तान्तरण हुन नसकेको बताइन्छ ।

पुरक सम्झौताको उल्लंघन र कोभिडको मार

भवन हस्तान्तरण हुन नसकेपछि दुवै पक्षबीच वि.सं. २०७८ मङ्सिर २८ गते पुरक सम्झौता गरियो, जसमा भवन हस्तान्तरणको मिति २०७८ असार १ कायम गर्ने प्रयास गरियो । तर, सो अवधिमा देशव्यापी रूपमा फैलिएको कोभिड–१९ को दोस्रो लहर र लकडाउनका कारण भवन पूर्ण रूपमा तयार भई व्यापारिक प्रयोजनका लागि हस्तान्तरण हुनै सकेन ।

व्यापार व्यवसाय ठप्प भएको र बैंक तथा वित्तीय संस्थाबाट कर्जा प्रवाह नभएको यस्तो गम्भीर आर्थिक मन्दीको समयमा नेपाल सरकार रक्षा मन्त्रालयले समेत भाडामा छुट दिन निर्देशन जारी गरेको थियो । सैनिक कोषको आफ्नै कार्यदलले भाडामा ५० प्रतिशत छुट दिने राय पेस गरेपनि निर्देशनालयका केही अधिकारीहरूको बदनियतका कारण व्यवसायीले पाउनुपर्ने उक्त कानुनी छुट रकम उपलब्ध गराइएन ।

प्रशासनको उल्झन

निर्माण कम्पनीका एकल शेयरधनी खगेन्द्र बुढामगरका अनुसार, खण्डहर अवस्थामा रहेको भवनलाई अर्बौँ रुपैयाँ निजी लगानी गरेर मासिक ५ करोड ६३ लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी भाडा उठ्ने सुनिश्चित व्यावसायिक केन्द्र बनाएपछि सैनिक कोषका केही अधिकारीहरूको ‘गिद्धे नजर’ यसमा परेको हो ।

कम्पनीले पटक–पटक पारदर्शी हिसाब मिलानका लागि लिखित अनुरोध गर्दा समेत त्यसलाई बेवास्ता गर्दै उल्टै पानी र बिजुलीको लाइन काट्ने, लिफ्ट प्रयोग गर्न नदिने र कम्पनीका कर्मचारीहरूमाथि कार्यस्थलमै भौतिक आक्रमण गर्नेसम्मका निकृष्ट कार्यहरू भएका छन् । जसले गर्दा व्यवसायी मानसिक र आर्थिक रूपमा पूर्णतः धराशयी हुने अवस्थामा पुगेका छन् ।

निष्पक्ष छानबिन र हिसाब फरफारकको माग

नेपाली सेनासँग लामो समयदेखि विकट भूगोल र ब्यारेकहरूमा समेत निर्माण कार्य गरी व्यावसायिक सम्बन्ध कायम राखेको यस कम्पनीले रक्षा मन्त्रालय, प्रधानसेनापति कार्यालय र बालाध्यक्ष विभागमा बोधार्थ दिँदै एक उच्चस्तरीय निष्पक्ष छानबिन टोली गठन गर्न माग गरेको छ । कम्पनीले सैनिक कल्याणकारी कोषलाई कुनै रकम तिर्नु बुझाउनु पर्ने बाँकी नरहेको, उल्टै कल्याणकारी कोषको तर्फबाट भएको सम्झौता उल्लंघन र अनाधिकृत रकम असुलीका कारण आफूले अर्बौँ रुपैयाँ क्षतिपूर्ति पाउनुपर्ने दाबी गरेको छ । राज्यको शक्तिशाली अंगको आडमा एउटा वैधानिक निर्माण व्यवसायीको निजी सम्पत्ति र लगानीमाथि गरिएको यो चरम दोहनले नेपालमा निजी क्षेत्रको लगानी कति असुरक्षित छ भन्ने गम्भीर प्रश्न खडा गरेको छ ।

भवन ठेक्कामा करिब २० करोड हिनामिना आरोप

काठमाडौँको न्यूरोड महाँकालस्थानस्थित सैनिक कल्याणकारी कोषको स्वामित्वमा रहेको व्यावसायिक भवन ठेक्का प्रकरणमा तत्कालीन सैनिक कल्याणकारी निर्देशनालयका उच्च अधिकारी र कर्मचारीहरूको मिलेमतोमा झण्डै २० करोड रुपैयाँ बराबरको ठूलो आर्थिक हिनामिना भएको गम्भीर आरोप लागेको छ । श्रीजयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रा। लि। का एकल शेयरधनी खगेन्द्र बुढामगरले सैनिक कल्याणकारी कोषका तत्कालीन उच्च अधिकारी र हालका प्रमुख अवकाशप्राप्त जर्नेल सुनिल राज विष्ट,कर्मचारीहरू नानिराम थापा र कर्णबहादुर तामाङ लगायतले शक्तिको दुरुपयोग गरी अर्बौँको निजी लगानी डुबाउन खोजेको आरोप लगाएका छन् ।

श्री जयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रालिबाट भवन व्यवस्थापन कार्यालयमा पदस्थापन भएका नानिराम थापा,कर्णबहादुर तामाङ लगायत त्यहाँ कार्यरत कर्मचारीहरुको मिलेमतोमा उक्त भवनमा श्री जयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रालिले उठाउनुपर्ने भाडा बिजुली महसुल र क्याम्प चार्ज असुल गरेको आरोप लागेको हो ।

त्यस्तै,यो टोलीले निर्माण व्यवसायी खगेन्द्र बुढामगरसँग मात्र होइन,त्यस भवनमा व्यवसाय गरिरहेका विभिन्न व्यापारीलाई नाम सारी तथा राम्रो लोकेशनको पसल उपलब्ध गराइदिने प्रलोभनमा पारी रकम उठाइरहेको बुढाको गम्भीर आरोप छ ।

त्यसैगरी बुढाका अनुसार यी पात्रहरुले अदालतलाई समेत विभिन्न माध्यमबाट दबाब सिर्जना गर्ने र मुद्दालाई कम्जोर बनाएर आफ्नो काला कर्तुतहरु लुकाउन खोजेको उनले बताएका छन् ।

कल्याणकारी निर्देशनालयले बोलपत्र आह्वान गर्दा भवनको नक्सा पास नै नभएको र महानगरको अवरोधका कारण निर्माण कम्पनीले समयमा काम सुरु गर्न नपाएको, भवन पूर्ण रूपमा निर्माण नै नभई र खण्डहर अवस्थामा रहँदा समेत निर्देशनालयले पुरै अवधिको पूर्ण भाडा दाबी गरी पत्र पठाउनु कानुनी रूपमा त्रुटिपूर्ण रहेको, कम्पनीले आफ्नै खर्चमा जडान गरेको ट्रान्सफर्मर, विद्युतीकरण, खानेपानी प्रणाली, र लिफ्ट जस्ता पूर्वाधारहरू कल्याणकारी भवन व्यवस्थापनले एकतर्फी रूपमा नियन्त्रणमा लिई व्यवसायीलाई प्रवेशमा रोक लगाएको आरोप लागेको छ ।

भवन व्यवस्थापनकै केही कर्मचारीहरूले व्यापारीहरूबाट सोझै करिब १ करोड ३५ लाख विद्युत महसुल र क्याम्प चार्ज उठाएको साथै २०७९ साल श्रावण,भदौ र असोज ५ गतेसम्मको पुरै भवन भाडा श्री जयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रालिको बैंक ग्यारेन्टीबाट असुल गरेको र त्यहाँ व्यवसायी गरिरहेका ब्यापारीहरुबाट समेत असुल गरी सो रकम हिसाबमा मिलान नगरी गायब पारेको अर्को गम्भिर आरोप पनि छ ।

कम्पनीको नाममा रहेको मिटर तथा बिलिङ सफ्टवेयर नक्कली हस्ताक्षर प्रयोग गरी अनाधिकृत रूपमा नामसारी गरिएको र कम्पनीले अर्बौँ खर्चेर बनाएका संरचनाहरू सहमति बिना भत्काएर दोहन गरिएको आरोप छ ।

त्यस्तै,अहिले यस विषयमा मानव अधिकार लगायतका स्वतन्त्र निकायहरुले वास्तविक छानबिन गरिरहेको र सर्वोच्च अदालतमा समेत मुद्दा चलिरहेको निर्माण व्यवसायी बुढा मगरले जानकारी दिए । उनका अनुसार सर्वोच्च अदालतले १५ श्रावणमा दुबैपक्षलाई छलफलका लागि बोलाएको हुँदा उक्त छलफलबाट सकारात्मक नतिजा आउने बुढा मगरले विश्वास गरेका छन् ।

articles.title: एनसेल अब सरकारको नाममा आउने, सर्वोच्चको बोल्ड फैसलापछि वालेन्द्रको परीक्षा शुरु
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । एनसेल निजी क्षेत्रको अग्रणी सञ्चार माध्यमको रुपमा स्थापित कम्पनी हो। तर, एनसेलले नेपालमा गरिरहेको व्यापार र सेवा प्रवाह भने विवादास्पद नै छ। कर प्रकरणदेखि अन्य विषयमा समेत लम्बेतान विवादमा फसेको एनसेलको सेयर किनबेचपछि भने यसबारेका प्रश्नको सवालमा सर्वोच्च अदालतको आदेशपछि थप कानूनी प्रष्टतासहित अवैध गतिविधिविरुद्ध नेपालले आफ्नो कानूनको कार्यान्वयन गर्न सक्षम छ भन्ने सन्देश दिएको छ ।

लामो समय कर विवादमा फसेको एनसेल नेपालको अग्रणी निजी क्षेत्रको टेलिकम सेवा प्रदायक बन्न पुग्यो। नेपालको टेलिकम क्षेत्रमा नविनताका निम्ति काम गरेको एनसेलले सञ्चारको क्षेत्रमा खेलेको भूमिकामाथि प्रश्न गर्ने ठाउँ छैन्।

अझं भन्नुपर्दा सरकारी स्वामित्वको नेपाल टेलिकमले दिने सेवालाई एनसेलले दिएको चुनौतीकै कारण सञ्चार क्षेत्रले नेपालमा राम्रो स्तरको सेवा प्रवाहमा काम गरेको पाइन्छ। तर, एनसेलको यो राम्रो पाटोसंगै विवाद भने अत्यन्तै महत्वपूर्ण छन्। हरेक वर्ष मनग्य आम्दानी पनि दिएको एनसेलले विदेशमा नोपलबाट ठूलो धनराशी पठाएको छ।

सेवासंगै मेवा पनि दिएको एनसेलले केहि विवाद यस्ता पनि भोग्यो, जुन नेपालको कानूनको प्रत्यक्ष उल्लङ्घन र राज्यविरुद्ध गरेको एकखाले अपराध नै हो। कर छली विवाद लामो समयसम्म लम्बिदा एनसेलले आफ्ना भौतिक संरचनामा क्षति व्यहोर्ने स्थिति बन्यो। अझं, तत्कालीन विप्लव नेतृत्वको नेकपाले एनसेलको कार्यालयमा बम विस्फोट गराएपछि सेक्युरिटी गार्डले ज्यान नै दिने स्थिति बन्यो। यसरी देशभरका विभिन्न क्षेत्रका भौतिक संरचनामा किन आक्रमण भए? यसका पछाडी कारण हुन्, एनसेलले नेपालको कानून पालना गर्न भन्दा बढि मुनाफा आर्जन गर्ने ध्येय राख्नु।

सेयर खरिदबिक्रीको घोटाला

एनसेलले गरेको सेयर खरिदबिक्री भने अस्वभाविकमात्रै थिएन, सार्वभौम मुलुकको स्वाधिनतामाथिको प्रहार नै थियो। नेपालले निर्माण गरेको कानून व्यवसायमैत्री थिएन भनेपनि त्यो कानून नेपालको सार्वभौमसत्तासंग जोडिएको विषय थियो।

नेपालको संसदले निर्माण गरेको कानून नेपालभित्र सबैलाई मान्य र बाध्यकारी हुन्छ। तर, एनसेलको हकमा यो लागू नहुने गरि गरिएको सेयर खरिदबिक्रीमा सर्वोच्चको झड्कापछि भने नेपालले आफ्नो कानूनको पालना निर्वाध गराउनसक्छ भन्ने प्रष्ट सन्देश दिएको छ ।

सेयर खरिदबिक्री अमान्य

सर्वोच्च अदालतका न्यायाधीशद्वय सपना प्रधान मल्ल र टेकप्रसाद ढुंगानाको संयुक्त इजलासले विवादास्पद सेयर खरिदबिक्रीलाई अमान्य र अस्वभाविक भन्दै खारेज गरिदिएको छ।

यसले एनसेलको अध्यक्ष बन्न पुगेका सतिसलाल आचार्य अब कर्मचारीको हैसियतमा पुगेका छन भने एनसेलको सेयर स्वामित्व रेनोल्ड होल्डिङ्स लिमिटेडको वास्तविक मालिक मलेसियन कम्पनी आजियाटाकै रहेको ठहर गरेको छ। सतिसलालको कम्पनी स्पेक्ट्रलाइट युकेले किनेको भनिएको ८० प्रतिशत सेयर अमान्य भएको छ ।

के भन्यो सर्वोच्चले ?

सर्वोच्च अदालतले एनसेलको सेयर स्वामित्व ६ अर्ब हाराहारीमा भएको कारोबारलाई अमान्य र अस्वभाविक भनेको छ । अदालतले सन् २०१६ मा करिब १ खर्ब ४३ अर्ब रुपैयाँमा खरिद गरिएको शेयरलाई अत्यन्तै न्यून मूल्यमा किनबेच गरिएको भन्नुलाई नै कानूनको उल्लङ्घनको रुपमा ठहर गरेको हो। सर्वोच्चले आदेशमा भनेको छ, ’शेयर खरीद बिक्री कारोबारको बारेमा विदेशी लगानी तथा प्रविधि हस्तान्तरण ऐन, २०७५ को दफा १९ को अभिलेख राख्ने व्यवस्थासँग आफूलाई अनुमति दिने, नियमन गर्ने विशेष कानूनको रूपमा रहेको दुर सञ्चार नियमावली, २०५४ को नियम १५ (१) (ट) को व्यवस्थालाई नजरअन्दाज गर्न मिल्ने देखिएन ।

प्रस्तुत संशोधित ऐ. नियम १५ ( १ ) (ट) तथा नेपाल दुर सञ्चार प्राधिकरण ( अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त व्यक्तिको शेयर खरीद बिक्री) विनियमावली, २०७६ को विनियम (१), (३) र विनियम ४ को खण्ड (क) लाई चुनौति दिएको अवस्था पनि रहेको छैन । अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त व्यक्ति विपक्षी एनसेल आजियाटा लिमिटेडको ८०% शेयर धारण गर्ने शेयरवाला आजियाटा इन्भेष्टमेन् (यु.के.) लिमिटेडले आफ्नो शेयर स्पेक्ट्रलाइट यु.के. लिमिटेडलाई मिति २०८० । ८ । १५ (तदनुसार १ डिसेम्बर २०२३) मा बिक्री गरेको तथ्यमा विवाद देखिदैन । उक्त शेयर कारोवार हुनु अगावै नेपाल दुर सञ्चार प्राधिकरणबाट पूर्व स्वीकृति लिनुपर्नेमा नलिएको, विपक्षीबाट पेस भएको लिखित जवाफमा शेयरधनीको शेयर खरीद बिक्री हुँदा प्राधिकरणबाट स्वीकृति लिनुपर्ने व्यवस्था नै छैन भन्ने जिकिर लिएको र मिति २०८० । ८ । १५ (तदनुसार डिसेम्वर १ सन् २०२३) मा भएको शेयर खरीद बिक्री सम्झौताको सम्बन्धमा मिति २०८०।११।१२ मा मात्र स्वीकृतिको लागि प्राधिकरणमा निवेदन पेस गरेको स्थिति देखिएकाले विपक्षी एनसेल आजियाटा लिमिटेडले दुर सञ्चार ऐन, २०५३, दुर सञ्चार नियमावली, २०५४ र नेपाल दुर सञ्चार प्राधिकरण (अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त व्यक्तिको शेयर खरीद बिक्री) विनियमावली, २०७६ र अनुमतिपत्रको शर्तसमेत अक्षरशः परिपालना गर्दै पारदर्शी र विधिसम्मत तरिकाले सेवा संचालन गर्नू भनी विपक्षी एनसेल आजियाटा लिमिटेडको नाममा निर्देशनात्मक आदेश जारी गरिदिएको छ ।’

यसरी हेर्दा अब एनसेलको सञ्चालन एनसेल आजियाटाले नै गर्नुपर्नेछ। यसरी हेर्दा सतिसलालले गरेको कारोबार अवैध ठहर भएको छ भने अब ससितलाल एनसेलको अध्यक्षभन्दा पनि कर्मचारी वा अन्य हैसियतमा पुग्ने भएका छन्।

अब सरकारीकरणको बाटो खुला

नेपालको दूरसञ्चार ऐनले निश्वित अवधिपछि निश्चित कानूनी बाटो पुरा नगरेमा टेलिकम कम्पनी नेपाल सरकारको नाममा स्वतः आउने व्यवस्था गरेको छ। जसअनुसार दूरसञ्चार ऐन, २०५३ को दफा ३३ अनुसार ५० प्रतिशतभन्दा बढी विदेशी लगानी भएका दूरसञ्चार कम्पनीहरूको अनुमतिपत्रको २५ वर्षे अवधि समाप्त भएपछि त्यसको स्वामित्व स्वतः नेपाल सरकारमा हस्तान्तरण हुने व्यवस्था गरेको छ ।

एनसेलले १६ भदौ २०६१ मा अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त गरेकाले १५ भदौ २०८६ मा यसको २५ वर्षे अवधि पुरा हुनेछ । जुन अवधिपछि एनसेलको सेयर स्वामित्वमा वैध वदलाव नआएमा सरकारीकरणको चरणमा प्रवेश गर्ने निश्वित छ ।

उसोतः एनसेल प्रकरणमा नेपाल प्रहरीको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्यूरो (सीआइबी)ले ठगी, आपराधिक विश्वासघात जस्ता विषयमा अनुसन्धान भने गरिरहेको छ। सर्वोच्चले एनसेलको सेयर स्वामित्व सरकारको नाममा आउने बाटो खुला गरिदिएपनि कानूनी बाटाहरु कसरी अघि बढ्छन्? सरकारी नीति कस्ता बन्छन भन्ने विषयले समेत यो विषयमा थप निर्धारण गर्नेछ ।

अमरेशको सक्रियता

तत्कालीन समयमा स्वतन्त्र रुपमा प्रतिनिधिसभामा निर्वाचित भएका अमरेशकुमार सिंहले एनसेलको सेयर खरिदबिक्रीलाई चुनौती दिदै सर्वोच्चमा रिट दर्ता गराए। अमरेश अहिले राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टीबाट कांग्रेस सभापति गगन थापालाई पराजित गर्दै फेरि सर्लाही निर्वाचन क्षेत्र नम्बर ४ बाट प्रतिनिधिसभा सदस्यमा निर्वाचित भइसकेका छन्।

उनै सिंहले सर्वोच्चमा एनसेल आजियाटा, दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरण, प्रधानमन्त्री कार्यालय, ठूला करदाता कार्यालय, कम्पनी रजिष्ट्रार जस्ता धेरै निकायलाई विपक्षी बनाएर रिट दर्ता गराएका थिए। यहि प्रकरणमा सर्वोच्चको फैसलाले एनसेलको सेयर खरिदबिक्रीलाई अवैध ठहर गरेको हो।

निर्णय अब सरकारको हातमा

नेपालमा विदेशी लगानीका सम्बन्धमा अनेक अफवाहहरु फैलिने गर्छन्। कतिपयले एनसेल प्रकरणले नेपालमा ठूला लगानी नआउने भन्दै यसलाई मोड्ने प्रयास समेत गरेको देखिन्छ। सरकारले पनि मध्यम वर्गलाई ठूलो प्रभाव पर्ने गरि काम गरिरहेको बेला विदेशी लगानीलाई नेपालको कानूनको पालना गर्ने र विवादको समाधानका निम्ति सहजीकरणको बाटो खोज्दै काम गर्ने वातावरण सिर्जना गर्नुपर्ने देखिन्छ ।

एनसेल कब्जा गर्ने सतिसलालसहितको टोलीले नै स्मार्ट टेलिकमको सम्पत्ति कौडीको भाउमा लिलाम सकारेको घटनाबाटै सरकारले कानूनको पालना गराउने र आवश्यक सहजीकरणसहित दण्ड र पुरस्कारको व्यवस्था गर्न आवश्यक देखिन्छ। तर, सरकारले यस्ता विषयलाई कसरी अघि लैजान्छ भन्ने चासो र केहि शंकाहरु भने देखिन्छन। यद्यपी अब कानूनविपरितका विषयलाई दण्ड र विदेशी लगानीलाई प्रोत्साहन गर्ने गरि काम गर्नुको विकल्प भने देखिन्न ।

articles.title: कोलकाताबाट २४ घण्टामै नेपालमा ढुवानी, व्यवसायी उत्साहित
articles.summary:
मोरङ । उद्घाटन भएको करिब ३ वर्षपछि विराटनगरस्थित एकीकृत जाँच चौकीसम्म कार्गो रेलको सेवा पुनः शुरु भएको छ । पारवहन सन्धीको प्रोटोकल संसोधन पछि विराटनगरको एकीकृत जाँच चौकीस्थित नेपालको कस्टम यार्डसम्म कार्गो रेल आएको हो ।

विराटनगर स्थित एकिकृत जाँच चौकीसम्म कार्गो रेलको सेवा पुनः शुरु भएको छ । तत्कालिन प्रधानमन्त्री पुष्पकमल दाहाल प्रचण्ड र भारतका प्रधानमन्त्री नरेन्द्र मोदीले २०८० साल जेठ १८ गते उद्घाटन गरेयता कार्गो रेल आउन सकेको थिएन ।

मोरङको नेमुवास्थित स्वस्तिक आयल इण्डष्ट्रिजले मगाएको तोरी बोकेका ४० वटा कन्टेनरसहितको कार्गो रेल नेपाल भंसार यार्डसम्म आएको हो । रेल आएपछि सुनसरी मोरङ औद्योगिक करिडोरका उद्योगी व्यवसायीहरु उत्साहित भएका छन् ।

कार्गो रेलबाट ढुवानी गर्दा ढुवानी लागत २५ देखि ३० प्रतिशत घट्ने, कोलकाता बन्दरगाहबाट विराटनगरसम्म २४ घण्टामा सामान आईपुग्ने र बाटोमा सामान चोरी हुने समस्या निराकरण हुने भएकाले अन्य क्षेत्रका उद्योगहरुसँग प्रतिस्पर्धा गर्न सहज हुने उद्योगी व्यवसायीहरुले बताएका छन् ।

भारत सरकार अन्र्तर्गतको कन्कोर अर्थात कन्टेनर कर्पोरेशन अफ इण्डिया लिमिटेडको कार्गाे रेलबाट सोमवार एनसिवाई अर्थात नेपाल कस्टम यार्ड सम्म मालवाहक रेल आएको हो ।

कन्कोरका प्रतिनिधि संजिव साहले हप्तामा दुई दिन कोलकाताबाट विराटनगरसम्म कार्गो रेल संचालन गर्ने र यसलाई आवश्यकता अनुसार बढाउदै लैजाने जानकारी दिए ।

पारवहन सन्धीको प्रोटोकल संसोधनपछि विराटनगरको एकीकृत जाँच चौकीस्थित नेपाल कस्टम यार्डसम्म कार्गो रेल आएको हो । कार्गो रेल संचालन पछि विराटनगर आएको कन्टेनर खाली फर्कने भएकाले यहाँबाट वस्तु निर्यातमा पनि सहजता आउने उद्योगी व्यवसायीहरुले बताएका छन् ।

articles.title: प्युजो मोटरसाइकल्स नेपालद्वारा ‘Soirée Francaise’ आयोजना: फ्रान्सेली संस्कृति र जीवनशैलीको अनुभव
articles.summary:
अग्नि ग्रुप अन्तर्गतको प्युजो मोटरसाइकल्स नेपालले ‘Soirée Française – A Night of French Elegance’ शीर्षकमा एक विशेष 'फ्रेन्च फाइन डाइनिङ' कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न गरेको छ। काठमाडौँस्थित ला टेरास (La Terrasse) मा आयोजना गरिएको उक्त कार्यक्रममा प्युजोका विशिष्ट ग्राहक, व्यावसायिक साझेदार तथा फ्रान्सेली संस्कृतिप्रति आत्मियता राख्ने अतिथिहरूको उपस्थिति रहेको थियो।

कार्यक्रमले फ्रान्सको समृद्ध सांस्कृतिक विरासत र त्यसको प्रेरणादायी भावनालाई सम्मान गर्दै आपसी सम्बन्धलाई अझ सुदृढ बनाउने उद्देश्य राखेको थियो।

विश्वकपमा फ्रान्सेली टोलीको भावनाबाट प्रेरित

सन् २०२६ को फिफा विश्वकपमा फ्रान्सेली टोलीले प्रदर्शन गरेको समर्पण, दृढता, उत्कृष्टता र एकताको भावनाबाट प्रेरित भई यो कार्यक्रम आयोजना गरिएको हो। खेलको नतिजाभन्दा माथि उठेर फ्रान्सेली खेल संस्कृतिको अदम्य भावना र त्यसको विरासतलाई सम्मान गर्नु कार्यक्रमको मुख्य पक्ष थियो। यी मूल्यहरू प्युजो ब्रान्डको दीर्घकालीन पहिचानसँग समेत मेल खाने भएकाले सोही भावनालाई कार्यक्रममा प्रतिबिम्बित गरिएको थियो।

नेटवर्किङ र प्रिमियम जीवनशैलीको अनुभव

कार्यक्रममा सहभागी अतिथिहरूले पेरिस-प्रेरित आकर्षक सजावट तथा आत्मीय वातावरणमा विविध परम्परागत फ्रेन्च परिकारको स्वाद लिँदै नेटवर्किङको अनुभव सँगालेका थिए। प्युजोको फ्रान्सेली सम्पदालाई झल्काउँदै आफ्ना ग्राहकहरूप्रति कृतज्ञता व्यक्त गर्न र नेपालमा प्युजो समुदायसँगको सम्बन्धलाई अझ मजबुत बनाउन यस अवसरले सहयोग पुर्‍याएको कम्पनीले जनाएको छ।

ग्राहक केन्द्रित प्रतिबद्धता

यस अवसरमा प्युजो मोटरसाइकल्स नेपालका प्रतिनिधिहरूले गुणस्तरीय गतिशीलता (मोबिलिटी) समाधानका साथै ग्राहकलाई अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय स्तरको जीवनशैली अनुभव प्रदान गर्ने र विश्वव्यापी रूपमा प्युजोले प्रतिनिधित्व गर्ने मूल्य एवम् परम्परालाई निरन्तर अघि बढाउने प्रतिबद्धता पुनः व्यक्त गरे।

कार्यक्रमको समापन फ्रान्सेली संस्कृति, मित्रता र उत्कृष्टताको साझा भावनाप्रति सम्मान व्यक्त गर्दै ‘टोस्ट’ (Toast) का साथ गरिएको थियो। सहभागीहरूले यस अविस्मरणीय अनुभवले प्युजो मोटरसाइकल्स नेपाल र ग्राहकहरूबीचको प्रिमियम सम्बन्धलाई अझ सुदृढ बनाएको विश्वास व्यक्त गरेका छन्

articles.title: A prime minister who does not call on the President
articles.summary:
Four months after taking office, Prime Minister Balendra Shah has maintained almost complete distance from Sheetal Niwas, leaving his relationship with President Ramchandra Paudel virtually non-existent except mandatory official ceremonies.

Apart from swearing-in events and state functions, Shah has avoided direct meetings with the President. Major decisions—such as Cabinet reshuffles, the summoning and prorogation of parliament, and issuance of ordinances—have all moved forward without the traditional one-on-one briefings expected between the head of government and the head of state.

At Sheetal Niwas, the official residence of the President, officials view this behaviour as a clear noncompliance of established democratic practices. A senior official at Sheetal Niwas, speaking on condition of anonymity, confirmed that PM Shah has not visited to discuss governance, policy, or state affairs since taking his oath.

The official expressed disappointment over the government's failure to present the annual performance report of the Council of Ministers. “Past prime ministers personally submitted the Cabinet's annual report to the President before it was forwarded to parliament. The report for the previous fiscal year, which was due by mid-July, has still not been submitted,” said the official.

According to the official, the constitutional framework requires the prime minister to remain accountable not only to Parliament but also to the head of state. “The prime minister must personally inform the President about the law and order situation in the country, economic situation, diplomatic activities, Cabinet decisions, and bills under consideration in Parliament. This obligation applies to executive authorities and heads of constitutional bodies alike. That is the essence of constitutionalism. By ignoring these duties, the prime minister signals a disregard for our democratic system and the constitution itself.”

Article 81 of the constitution explicitly directs the prime minister to inform the President about Cabinet decisions, bills to be introduced in the federal parliament, specific details requested by the President, and current domestic conditions or foreign affairs.

Furthermore, Rule 36(A) of the Government of Nepal (Work Performance) regulation details nine specific areas for presidential updates. Beyond the four core constitutional points, these include treaties with foreign countries, the annual budget, major internal security developments, the government's policies and programmes, and decisions based on National Security Council recommendations.

While neither document sets a rigid timetable for face-to-face meetings, standard practice dictates that the prime minister consults the President whenever important national issues arise.

Recent unrest in Sunsari district offers a stark example. Under the governing rules, major security developments must be reported directly to Sheetal Niwas. Yet, rather than the prime minister providing the briefing, ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party Chairman Rabi Lamichhane visited President Paudel on Wednesday following an all-party meeting to discuss the situation. Lamichhane had previously briefed the President on June 8 after returning from India.

Opposition leaders have openly criticised the prime minister's behaviour. During Wednesday's all-party meeting, Nepali Congress chief Gagan Kumar Thapa voiced strong objections to the prime minister's conspicuous absence from key discussions.

The Prime Minister's Secretariat dismisses claims of friction. When asked via WhatsApp about the growing distance between the two leaders, Asim Shah, political advisor to the prime minister, offered a curt reply: "That is simply not the case."

Another member of the prime minister's secretariat rejected rumours that Prime Minister Shah had called for the President's resignation, calling such reports entirely baseless.

Despite those official denials, records show a growing physical and operational gap. Prime Minister Shah has visited Sheetal Niwas only six times over the past four months, with every visit strictly confined to mandatory state functions.

His visits include attending his own Cabinet swearing-in on March 26, the Speaker of the House of Representatives' oath on April 4, the National Assembly Vice-Chair's oath on April 6, a Cabinet reshuffle on the same day, Chief Justice Manoj Kumar Sharma's swearing-in on May 19, and a Cabinet reshuffle and portfolio reassignment on June 9.

No public record exists of any private meeting called by the prime minister to brief the President on national affairs.

Rajendra Dahal, former press advisor to Nepal's first President Ram Baran Yadav, considers the public debate over this gap deeply troubling for state stability.

“When the executive ignores the head of state, it reflects a collapse of trust. That inevitably pushes the country into further institutional breakdown,” said Dahal. “The prime minister serves as the President's chief political advisor and primary source of information. Without those briefings, the President is left completely uninformed, creating confusion at the highest levels of government.”

Dahal noted that convention requires the prime minister to meet the President at least once a month, even during quiet periods. “During crises, updates should occur daily. If the prime minister is unavailable, a Cabinet minister should be dispatched. The current lack of trust between these two key offices is a serious political problem.”

Key government moves have proceeded without direct consultation. On April 21, the cabinet decided to summon the second parliamentary session for April 30 and the President issued the call accordingly. But just two days later, the government abruptly asked the President to cancel the call, only to ask for another session on May 10 after issuing ordinances, including one on the Constitutional Council. Sheetal Niwas officials noted that the prime minister never met the President to explain the reasoning behind those sudden reversals.

President Paudel had explicitly sought a personal consultation regarding the Constitutional Council Ordinance. Sources confirm that Sheetal Niwas sent word to the prime minister's official residence in Baluwatar. After the prime minister declined to meet, the President sent the ordinance back on May 4, requesting reconsideration.

On May 5, Prime Minister Shah sent a written reply to the President's queries but still chose not to meet him in person. "An earlier version of the Constitutional Council Bill had been returned by the President to parliament,” said a senior presidential staff member. “When the ordinance arrived without addressing those original concerns, the President asked for a face-to-face discussion. The message was delivered, but the prime minister simply did not show up.”

In another departure from convention, the Cabinet decided that the President, rather than the prime minister, would deliver the official address on Republic Day. Former Chief Secretary Suman Aryal delivered the Cabinet decision directly to Sheetal Niwas without the prime minister's presence. Since the declaration of the republic in 2008, prime ministers had consistently delivered the address at Tundikhel. This year, President Paudel delivered it instead.

Constitutional experts emphasise that smooth collaboration between both offices is vital for parliamentary democracy. Senior Advocate Chandra Kanta Gyawali stated that executive actions must rely on close consultation. “The constitutional president performs duties based on the recommendation and consent of the prime minister. Regular meetings are necessary to review state actions, and because these consultations are political, they remain outside judicial review. The constitution requires a close working relationship between both offices. If they are not even meeting, it points to a serious rift that damages the parliamentary system.”

articles.title: Nepali football in free fall as FIFA ban, league shutdown drive players away
articles.summary:
Nepal’s top-tier domestic club football competition, the Martyr’s Memorial ‘A’ Division League, has not been organised for over 1,100 days—since Church Boys United lifted the title, on June 10, 2023, on their debut in the top flight.

The inability to organise the club football cycle—A, B and C Division and C-Division Qualifier—timely has led an increasing number of footballers to leave the game—and the country—in search of other sources of livelihood abroad.

Things took a turn for the worse when, on June 24, FIFA, the global footballing body, suspended Nepali football for an indefinite period. Stakeholders now worry that football in Nepal—once the country’s most loved game—is dying a slow death.

“I don’t think Nepali football has ever hit a lower point,” says Bal Gopal Maharjan, a veteran coach and former footballer.

Maharjan recalls a comparable period of uncertainty around 2000, when two parallel ANFA factions existed. But even that, he notes, was not as dire as the current situation.

A legend of his playing era, Maharjan went on to become one of the most successful coaches in both domestic and international football. His primary concern now is the regression of Nepali football’s competitive standards.

Ever since FIFA suspended ANFA, citing third-party interference, all footballing activity has effectively ground to a halt. Stakeholders remain silent.

Without regular matches, the danger is not just losing players, but a dramatic decline in the country’s overall football standard. “At the South Asian level, we could at least go toe-to-toe and mount a strong challenge,” Maharjan recalls. “We entered every tournament as title contenders. That might no longer be the case. As players leave, it will directly hit performance levels.”

To make matters worse, there is no clarity on when Nepal will next play international football. The last time Nepal’s men’s team played international football was on March 31, in the Asian Cup Qualifiers against Laos.

Had everything been on track, the national team would currently be preparing for the SAFF Championship. Head coach Guglielmo Arena had even arrived in Kathmandu for that purpose, but returned home after resigning from the role, citing the FIFA ban and uncertainty of football’s future in the country.

The South Asian tournament is scheduled to run from November 4 to 17 in Dhaka, Bangladesh. But while SAFF announced the dates, it did not detail how the competition would be structured without Nepal, one of their biggest audiences.

It is clear that the regional body is waiting to see when FIFA lifts its ban on Nepal. If a concrete resolution is not reached soon, the SAFF Championship could be held without Nepal for the first time in history.

And without football, more players are disappearing.

“Right now, even the remaining players lack both match exposure and experience. Football isn’t just played on the pitch. It’s a mental game,” Maharjan adds. “It is tough for everyone—from coaches to referees—but players are suffering the most as the income dries up; everyone searches for something else. My biggest fear is that we will see more players leaving the country.”

When Arena was still in Nepal, he had only one message: football must keep happening, and national team training must run continuously. Regular training maintains a team’s baseline performance, and without it, he warned, the situation would become precarious.

But with over three years of no regular domestic football followed by a FIFA suspension, Nepali football has hit rock bottom. It means that hundreds of footballers have seen years pass without their main source of livelihood.

“We are in constant contact with the players. Everyone is frustrated and uncertain about their future,” says Bikram Lama, president of the Nepal Football Players Association. “Right now, football players have zero income. Everyone is effectively unemployed. If this continues, players will be forced to look for alternative careers.”

However, Lama maintained that efforts are being made from their side to end the crisis.

The last official domestic competition held was the National League, a separate event in the football cycle that saw its format changed only to shut the critics. It is initially a 10-team tournament—comprising the top four teams of the President League and the top six teams from the previous ‘A’ Division League.

However, when the National League commenced on January 14, it saw 17 teams as ANFA caved in to the pressure from the remaining A-Division clubs, who kept pressuring for the regular division league football, and allowed all of them to participate. Had Himalayan Sherpa Club also participated, the number would have been 18.

But the National League never concluded as it got postponed on March 18 with 38 of the 136 matches remaining. Not only the National League, but even the Martyr’s Memorial ANFA Women’s League got postponed on March 19, only a day after the tournament began.

The tussle between the NSC and ANFA also saw the national women’s team lose their participation in the FIFA Series. The players, who were training with uncertainty, felt lucky when they could participate at the SAFF Women’s Championship in Goa, India, last month.

But now, it is uncertain when Nepal will next play an international match, let alone the resumption of the domestic football cycle.

“Since the National League and Women’s League were postponed, almost all players have been left without an income,” Lama said. “Mid-tier players have largely disappeared from the setup, while national team members remain conflicted about their next steps, reluctant to speak publicly about their future plans.”

Insiders acknowledge a grim reality: by the time ANFA’s suspension is lifted and football returns to the pitch, finding enough active players could prove difficult. It was already difficult for the teams in the National League.

According to ANFA’s own data, there are 60 national team players across the men’s and women’s squads, 92 ANFA-licensed coaches, and 14 FIFA referees.

Across the division cycle, there would have been 1,260 registered players. Similarly, the domestic women’s scene would have seen at least 360 active female footballers.

A few days ago, several clubs released a joint press statement emphasising that thousands of players, coaches, officials, and dependents are suffering severe hardship.

Among them was Sankata Club. Its president, Indra Man Tuladhar, insists that domestic football must keep moving regardless.

“FIFA hasn’t banned domestic football,” notes Tuladhar, who is also the chief executive officer of ANFA. “At the very least, domestic tournaments should continue.”

Clubs had signed players on three-month contracts for the now-halted National League, but those contracts have expired. Aside from departmental team players, almost no footballers are currently under professional contract.

“However, under the National Sports Council’s latest directive, even domestic football cannot take place. FIFA’s ban only restricts international participation. It is high time domestic football got moving again. When the FIFA ban will be lifted is one thing, but that shouldn't stop domestic football from running.”

Meanwhile, former national team player Bishal Shrestha currently holds a leadership position, vice chairperson, at the NSC. Shrestha effectively retired from playing upon joining the council—prior to which he was one of domestic football’s longest-serving players.

“We are certainly worried about the players,” Shrestha says. “We are actively trying to find solutions to this crisis in Nepali football. Something needs to be done to keep domestic football active, but for concrete steps to be taken, we simply have to wait a little longer.”

How long? Nobody knows. Even the government, which has been directed by FIFA to ensure that ANFA can operate independently for the suspension to be lifted, has remained mostly silent about it.

articles.title: Habitat concerns grow as Nepal counts a record 429 tigers
articles.summary:
Nepal’s tiger population has hit a record of 429, according to the latest national count of the wild animal made public on Wednesday, marking another milestone in the country's globally recognised conservation efforts while raising fresh concerns over habitat management, human-wildlife conflict and the carrying capacity of protected areas.

The Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation unveiled the report in Kathmandu in the presence of Minister for Agriculture and Forests Gita Chaudhary on the occasion of World Tiger Day observed every year on July 29.

The census recorded 74 more wild tigers than the previous nationwide count conducted in 2022, when the country recorded 355 big cats.

The latest census found tiger numbers increasing in all major protected areas except Bardiya National Park, long regarded as one of the country’s best destinations for tiger sightings. Chitwan National Park and its buffer zone, the country's largest tiger habitat, registered the highest population of tigers at 145. As per the 2022 count, there were a total of 128 tigers in Chitwan.

Hari Bhadra Acharya, information officer at the Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation, said Bardiya was the only protected area where tiger numbers declined.

The census, carried out between December 31, 2025, and April 23, 2026, using camera traps, also recorded significant increases elsewhere. Parsa National Park's tiger population rose to 71 from 41 and Banke National Park’s number climbed from 25 to 51 while Shuklaphanta National Park recorded 50 big cats, up from 36. Bardiya saw its tiger numbers drop from 125 to 112.

The latest figures sustain a remarkable conservation story. Around 2000, Chitwan had only about 60 tigers. The number climbed to 91 in 2009 and reached 120 in the 2013 survey before dropping to 93 in 2018.

Conservationists are elated with the results, saying that they reflected years of investment in habitat restoration, anti-poaching operations, prey recovery and cross-border cooperation with India.

“The increase in tiger numbers is encouraging not only for conservation but also for the country’s tourism industry,” said Baburam Lamichhane, a wildlife researcher specialising in tiger ecology. "It strengthens Nepal's reputation as a global conservation success. Past experience also shows that an increase in tiger numbers does not automatically mean an increase in human casualties."

Tiger conservation has become one of Nepal's strongest international environmental credentials. In 2022, Nepal doubled its wild tiger population from the 121 recorded in 2009, achieving the global TX2 target set at the 2010 St Petersburg Tiger Summit four years ahead of schedule.

Dil Bahadur Pun, chief conservation officer at the Chitwan National Park, said future programmes would focus on sustaining the growing population through better habitat management and closer cooperation with local communities.

“We will continue conservation programmes by incorporating community concerns alongside scientific recommendations,” said Pun. “Habitat management and long-term conservation planning will become even more important as tiger numbers increase.”

Shivaji Gayak, chairman of the Buffer Zone Management Committee under the Chitwan National Park, said local residents remained concerned that more tigers could lead to more attacks on people and livestock. “That fear exists in many communities. But if we continue raising awareness and reduce people's dependence on forests, human casualties can be minimised,” said Gayak.

Conservationists suggest that Nepal should now look beyond celebrating higher tiger numbers and use the achievement to strengthen nature-based tourism.

“We should think about how to generate greater benefits by allowing more tourists to see tigers. Many visitors are willing to spend significantly for a tiger-viewing experience. We need targeted plans and programmes to attract such tourists,” said Naresh Subedi, former member secretary of the National Trust for Nature Conservation (NTNC).

He attributed the rise in tiger numbers to improved habitat conservation and management, an increase in prey species, stronger anti-poaching measures, the expansion of protected areas and the development of wildlife corridors linking Nepal and India.

Experts, however, warned that the growing tiger population also presents new management challenges. Bhagawan Dahal, Nepal country representative of the Zoological Society of London, said habitat management would become increasingly important to minimise human-tiger conflict.

“If the right measures are implemented in time, losses caused by tigers can be reduced,” said Dahal. “Research shows that tigers are less likely to leave well-managed habitats. At the same time, providing alternative livelihood opportunities to communities living around parks and forests can significantly reduce conflict.”

Dahal suggested that the government should formulate a long-term national policy for tiger management as the population continues to grow.

Conservationists have also called for a debate on whether Nepal's existing protected areas can support a larger tiger population. While some argue the country is nearing its ecological carrying capacity, wildlife expert Hem Sagar Baral said Nepal could sustain between 400 and 500 tigers given the current availability of prey, improved grassland management and the combined habitats of national parks, buffer zones and surrounding forests.

Human-tiger conflict declines in Chitwan though rife elsewhere

Marichman Bhandari, 62, of Banke’s Rapti Sonari Rural Municipality-1 was grazing his livestock on January 2 when a tiger dragged him away and killed him in front of his companions. Less than two-and-a-half months later, Indra Bahadur Khatri, 30, of Rapti Sonari-9 was fatally attacked while cutting grass in a local community forest. Earlier, in late December last year, Dhansari Rawat, 42, of Salyan’s Kalimati Rural Municipality-7 and Chandra Bahadur Khaptadi, 65, of Kalimati-6, also lost their lives in separate tiger attacks.

The deaths underline the growing challenge of managing human-tiger conflict even as Nepal celebrates remarkable gains in tiger conservation.

According to the NTNC, 10 people were killed in tiger attacks in the last fiscal year of 2025-26. It was the first rise in fatalities after four consecutive years of decline. Four deaths occurred around Banke National Park, three in Parsa National Park, two in Bardiya National Park and one near Chitwan National Park.

Leopard attacks claimed another nine lives in Bardiya during the same period. Over the past eight years, 85 people have been killed in tiger attacks across Nepal.

Acharya said the increase in such incidents suggests that conservation efforts still have shortcomings. “We cannot change the behaviour of tigers, but we can certainly change our own,” said Acharya. “The next phase of conservation should therefore focus on changing the behaviour of local communities.”

Acharya said human-wildlife conflict is not one-sided. While tigers sometimes kill people and livestock, humans also retaliate by poisoning or trapping tigers. Contrary to popular belief, he said, healthy tigers do not normally attack humans. Most incidents involve old, injured or displaced animals that have become unable to hunt their natural prey.

“If such tigers can be identified and rescued in time, many conflicts can be prevented,” said Acharya. He also stressed the need to reduce people's dependence on forests by creating alternative livelihood opportunities. Many residents still enter forests daily to collect fodder, mushrooms, wild vegetables and fiddlehead ferns, increasing the likelihood of encounters with wildlife.

The tiger is found in only 13 countries worldwide.

Following the rise in tiger numbers in 2022, many people in Chitwan feared that a larger population of the predator would inevitably lead to more attacks. The latest figures, however, tell a different story. Chitwan National Park recorded no human fatality from tiger attacks in its buffer zone in the last fiscal year, according to Abinash Thapa Magar, information officer at the Park.

Communities have also adopted practical measures to minimise risk. Raju Silwal, chairman of the Kumroj Buffer Zone Community Forest, said residents are now allowed to enter forests only after 9 am, following an earlier fatal assault on a person collecting grass.

“We have fixed entry and exit times, designated separate grass-cutting areas and cleared vegetation to improve visibility,” Silwal said. “We also regularly educate forest users on how to avoid wildlife attacks.”

Gentle and shy by nature

Long-held assumptions about tiger behaviour are being challenged as the growing tiger population reveals new ecological patterns, according to conservationists.

Ashok Ram, chief conservation officer at Bardiya National Park, said the traditional belief that a male tiger requires about 50 square kilometres of territory and a female around 30 square kilometres no longer reflects conditions in the wild. Spread over 968 square kilometres, Bardiya National Park is home to 112 tigers, leaving an average of just seven to eight square kilometres of habitat per animal.

Field observations suggest that one male tiger often shares a territory with up to three females within an area of eight to 10 square kilometres. “If the females produce cubs, the density increases even further. The reality we are witnessing today does not match what we learned from ecological theory,” said Ram.

A tigress usually gives birth to two to four cubs. Researchers have also observed family groups living together more frequently, challenging the long-held view that tigers are strictly solitary animals. The gestation period ranges from 93 to 102 days.

Ajit Tumbahamphe, chief of the National Trust for Nature Conservation's Bardiya office, described tigers as naturally gentle and shy animals. “A healthy tiger does not deliberately hunt people. Most attacks involve old or injured animals that can no longer catch their natural prey and therefore turn to livestock or, in rare cases, humans,” said Tumbahamphe. He said the presence of tigers indicates a healthy ecosystem with abundant forests and prey species.

articles.title: Government yet to finalise ride-hailing rules as disputes over fares persist
articles.summary:
The government led by Balendra Shah had pledged to fast-track regulations for Nepal's rapidly expanding ride-hailing industry. Instead, the proposed framework has become mired in the same delays that stalled previous administrations.

Government officials involved in the process say the draft has been held up by disagreements over fare caps, commission limits and the use of privately registered vehicles, with ride-hailing platforms, transport operators and other stakeholders unable to reach a consensus.

More than three months after the proposed Digital Mobility Service Operation Standards, 2026 reached the Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport, it remains under review.

The government has struggled to reconcile competing interests before granting final approval, at least three officials familiar with the process told the Post.

A senior official at the Department of Transport Management said the draft is still undergoing consultations at the ministry.

"The digital mobility sector is technically complex, and every stakeholder—from ride-sharing companies and drivers to transport operators—has its own concerns. Reaching a consensus has therefore become difficult," the official said on condition of anonymity.

"While addressing the concerns of service providers and drivers, we must also protect consumers' rights."

According to officials, discussions have focused primarily on fare structures, commission rates and other operational provisions with major ride-hailing platforms, including Uber, Yango and other operators.

Under the proposed standards, the government plans to cap base fares at Rs25 per kilometre for two-wheelers and Rs55 per kilometre for four-wheelers. Night fares could rise by up to 20 percent, depending on operating conditions.

The draft also limits the commission digital platforms can charge to a maximum of 10 percent of each fare, with the remainder going to drivers.

"The ministry even proposed implementing some of the pricing provisions on a trial basis, but most ride-hailing companies opposed the idea, citing technical and financial complications," another department official said.

Another contentious issue is whether privately registered vehicles with red number plates should be allowed to provide commercial ride-hailing services.

Public transport operators have argued that if such vehicles are permitted to operate commercially, they should carry distinct identification markings.

Officials involved in drafting the standards say no consensus has been reached on the issue.

The Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport published the draft for public consultation on April 20.

Prepared by the Department of Transport Management, the proposal defines ride-sharing and ride-hailing services for the first time in Nepal while establishing licensing procedures, fare ceilings, safety requirements and compliance mechanisms.

The draft introduces the broader concept of "digital mobility service", covering app-based and web-based transport platforms that connect passengers with vehicles on demand.

It also includes several provisions aimed at improving safety and social protection. Digital mobility companies would be required to provide life insurance for drivers and riders, enrol them in the Social Security Fund, and operate 24-hour emergency response and grievance-handling systems staffed by trained personnel.

To improve passenger safety, particularly for women, the draft requires platforms to allow female passengers to choose female drivers or riders.

It also proposes strict penalties for harassment, reckless driving, operating outside the digital platform and driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs. Under a zero-tolerance policy, service providers would be required to cooperate with authorities to ensure accountability and compensation for victims.

The proposal further calls for the creation of an accident fund financed through a one percent deduction from passenger fares and a 0.5 percent contribution from the daily earnings of service providers. The fund would compensate passengers, drivers and riders injured in accidents.

The draft defines ride-sharing as multiple passengers travelling in the same vehicle in the same direction to improve efficiency, reduce costs and ease traffic congestion. Ride-hailing, meanwhile, is defined as booking a vehicle—with or without a driver—through a digital platform for private use with integrated payment and tracking systems.

The government's effort to regulate the sector follows years of disputes over the legal status of app-based transport services.

When Gandaki Province introduced its Ride-sharing (Regulation and Management) Regulation in May last year, public transport operators launched protests that disrupted transport services across the province. The province formally implemented the regulation in February after months of uncertainty.

The proposed standards are expected to provide Nepal's first comprehensive regulatory framework for ride-hailing and ride-sharing services after nearly a decade of rapid but largely unregulated growth.

The absence of a clear legal framework has left passengers vulnerable to inconsistent pricing, safety risks and weak grievance mechanisms, with no dedicated authority to handle complaints.

Reports of unfair fares, misconduct and passenger exploitation, particularly during emergencies and peak travel periods, have further eroded public trust in digital ride-hailing services.

In January 2019, the government cracked down on ride-hailing platforms like Tootle and Pathao, but public pressure forced it to back down as the ride-hailing apps had changed the way Nepalis travelled.

Subsequently, in February 2020, the Patan High Court ordered the government to regulate ride-hailing services.

The ride-sharing service was then listed as a service-oriented industry under the Industrial Enterprises Act 2020.

Bagmati Province declared ride-hailing services legal in June 2022, but it did not issue any guidelines or policy. Ride-hailing companies were permitted to operate mobile apps by registering with the Transport Department.

The Motor Vehicles and Transport Management Act 1993 has mentioned that vehicles registered for private use should not be used for public transportation. The law also bars vehicle owners from using their vehicles for other than declared purposes.

The first Nepali ride-sharing app was launched in 2017.

articles.title: End attacks against health workers, keep health services running
articles.summary:
On Saturday, Dr Pramod Ram, a doctor at Narayani Hospital in Birgunj, was assaulted by relatives of a 45-year-old patient who died while undergoing treatment in the hospital’s emergency ward. The attackers also vandalised hospital property and threatened other health workers. The incident prompted the hospital to suspend services, with all staff resigning en masse in protest.

The Nepal Medical Association, an umbrella organisation of medical and dental doctors, supported the protest by halting all non-emergency health services nationwide. While the strike was withdrawn on Wednesday evening, hundreds of thousands of patients were already deprived of medical care on Tuesday and Wednesday. Patients ultimately bear the brunt of such disruptions. Those who reached hospitals and health centres after travelling long distances are forced to return without treatment. People from low-income backgrounds, many of whom have to take loans or borrow money even to afford medical expenses, are hit the hardest.

Ceasing health services, therefore, cannot be justified under any circumstances. Hundreds of thousands of patients cannot be penalised for the wrongdoing of a few individuals. Moreover, suspending health services is illegal. The Health Service Act categorically recognises medical services as essential services that cannot be halted. Similarly, the Public Health Service Act states that no citizen shall be deprived of health services. By suspending essential services, the association has not only increased the hardships faced by patients but has also challenged the legal provisions governing healthcare delivery.

This, however, does not mean that attacks and threats against doctors and health workers should be overlooked. Physical assaults on medical professionals are criminal acts that require immediate legal action. The fact that around 90 incidents of physical attacks and assaults against health workers have taken place within a period of just 10 months highlights the urgency of the issue and demands swift intervention.

Ensuring proper security arrangements in the health sector must be a top priority for the government. Doctors and health workers are there to save and treat patients, not to harm them. Patients and their relatives, therefore, need to have faith in them. However, negligence on the part of doctors and health workers cannot be ruled out. There are bodies responsible for investigating such cases and taking appropriate action. Manhandling doctors and health workers is not the solution. In several instances, the compulsion for junior staff to handle complicated cases, coupled with inadequate resources, has led to unwanted treatment outcomes. It is the state that needs to address these shortcomings.

Medical facilities should be a safe space for doctors and health workers to work, while patients also have the right to receive proper treatment. Both can go hand in hand. Ensuring uninterrupted health services, strengthening security, and holding attackers accountable are of utmost importance. The situation in which health professionals have to work in constant fear, and health services are disrupted under any pretext, should end once and for all.

articles.title: The future of Tamil politics in Sri Lanka
articles.summary:
The Tamil political parties of Sri Lanka, namely All Ceylon Makkal Congress (ACMC), the Ceylon Workers’ Congress (CWC), Democratic Tamil National Alliance (DTNA), Ilankai Tamil Arasu Kachchi (ITAK), Sri Lanka Muslim Congress (SLMC) and Tamil Progressive Alliance (TPA), collectively raised their voices for Tamil political aspirations that have remained unresolved due to a lack of political will within majoritarian politics. On July 24, they decided to work on issues where there is consensus while maintaining their separate political identities, policies and positions. They have already met the President and plan to meet the opposition next, followed by a meeting with the diplomatic community to appraise their position. President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, in his election manifesto, underlined the need for a new constitution to fulfil Tamil political aspirations and received overwhelming support from Tamil voters.

Interestingly, each time the political issues concerning the Sri Lankan Tamils are raised, the Tamil parties state their demands with a preamble that they stand for United Sri Lanka, so their demand is not misconstrued as ‘separatism’. This is important because Tamil politics was hijacked by hardliners who espoused a separate state as the culmination of their long-standing grievances and as a separate ‘nation’. The unitary state of Sri Lanka is also mentioned in the Indo-Lanka Accord of 1987 when the two countries worked out a political solution that had festered for long. The Accord was important especially after the July 1983 massacre of Tamils in Colombo, which led to the evacuation of the Tamil population to Jaffna, underlining that Tamils can only be safe where their community is in the majority and shattering their faith in the state’s ability and willingness to protect them. Many Sri Lankans refer to the events of July 1983 as ‘Black July’. The separatists rejected the Accord at the time of signing. However, much water has flowed under the bridge since then.

The removal of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) through a war that Sri Lankan forces fought valiantly in 2009 opened up new vistas to move forward on this issue and seek a lasting solution. While some progress has been made post-war in terms of rehabilitation and the return of some land occupied by the armed forces, the recovery of skeletons from the Chemmani mass graves—suspected of having been killed extrajudicially—has reopened old wounds. This has been compounded by the delay in implementing constitutional reforms to address the political issues affecting the Tamils.

The Tamil political parties have historically been divided in their approach to Tamil political aspirations. Moreover, the Tamils are divided as Sri Lankan Tamils, hill or plantation Tamils (also known as the Malaiyaga Tamil community) and Tamil-speaking Muslims. The latter consider themselves ethnically separate. Each party has tried to maintain a separate identity and has disagreed with others.

While some Tamil political parties were co-opted by the Rajapakse government—which was in power during the war and remained in power till 2015—they sought an economic solution to Tamil grievances based on the notion that economic development and employment opportunities would set aside political aspirations or make them marginal to Tamil politics post-war. The once powerful Tamil National Alliance (TNA), ably led by R Sampathan of the Ilankai Tamil Arasu Katchi (ITAK), is no longer a dominant force to reckon with in Tamil politics. After Sampathan’s death, internal divisions within the ITAK became apparent. The division between S Sritharan, the party’s president, and MA Sumanitharan, who was close to Sampathan, also came to light during the 2024 Presidential election over their support for the Tamil Presidential candidate, P Ariyanethran.

While the Tamils of the North and the East have been divided, the Sri Lanka Muslim Congress also saw divisions in 2002, with the party’s split and the formation of ACMC, which has a strong presence in the North and East. With the patronage of the then Rajapakse government, a surrendered militant, Karuna Amman, one-time trusted ally of V Prabhakaran, who headed the LTTE, formed Tamil Makkal Viduthalai Pulikal (TMVP), splitting the Tamil vote in the East. The Eelam People’s Revolutionary Liberation Front (EPRLF) broke away, citing ITAK dominance within the coalition as an issue in 2015. In 2020, the Tamil Eelam Liberation Organisation (TELO) and People’s Liberation Organisation of Tamil Eelam (PLOTE) also pulled out of this political conglomeration. The Thamizh Makkal Kootani (TMK) is another party established by former Chief Minister of Northern Province, CV Wigneswaran, who accused ITAK of abandoning the cause of Tamils. Similarly, the Ceylon Workers Congress (CWC), which represented plantation Tamils, split in 1989 with the formation of the Up-Country People’s Front (UCPF), another faction, which, after many permutations and combinations, has now formed the Tamil Progressive Alliance (TPA), representing mainly Tamils living in other parts of Sri Lanka, beyond North and East where they have historically lived.

In the past, some of the Sri Lankan political parties have portrayed these parties, mainly the TNA and the ITAK, as espousing a separatist agenda as they worked with the LTTE even to operate in Tamil-dominated North and East. As the LTTE was dominant, none of the political parties could think of operating independently of LTTE patronage and getting elected, which was evident in the 2005 election that the LTTE boycotted. This division in Tamil political parties has always helped the ruling alliance. They also realise that without the support of political parties whose constituencies are predominantly Sinhalese and of a ‘southern consensus’, it is impossible for them even to secure a modicum of devolution.

While some of the issues of militarisation, such as the release of land occupied by the military, have made progress, the larger issue of constitutional reform is to be addressed as the government has failed to move forward. This is one of the reasons why the National People’s Power (NPP) share of the vote in the local election was reduced to 43 percent from the 61 percent it had received during the Parliamentary election two years ago. The Tamil parties’ better show in the local election reflects the community’s disillusionment with the NPP’s inability to address their concerns. While divisions within Tamil political parties strengthen the hand of ruling parties, the NPP’s assumption of power has given hope for new politics in Sri Lanka.

articles.title: Why Nepal must dare to dream of space
articles.summary:
It was April 25, 2015, the day a 7.8-magnitude earthquake struck Nepal. I was asking my father to check my homework when the bookshelves toppled. A falling vase cut my sister’s hand. For weeks, countless Nepalis, including my family, slept on the open ground because we did not trust the walls around and the floor underneath us. The vast open sky was the only thing I considered safe. Lying there one night, I remember feeling, “You are so small.”

Survival and scarcity are the real coordinates of life in Nepal. They shape what is considered practical, urgent and acceptable to want. I understand why the argument against space starts there. But if that is where it starts, it should not be where it ends. Because space was already working above us.

In the immediate aftermath of the earthquake that killed nearly 9,000 people, satellites and mapping systems from international satellite imagery providers like Planet and Digital Globe helped responders understand damage, roads, settlements, rescue plans and risk across Nepal. Weather data, communications and navigation systems also depended on infrastructure orbiting above us. Nepal did not send those satellites. We used them. We had no choice.

That is the version of space most people in developing and least developed countries miss. Popular culture shows space as just rockets, astronauts and science fiction. However, it also includes weather forecasting, disaster response, telecommunications, agriculture, land use, border monitoring, aviation, banking, television, GPS, internet connectivity and climate data.

When a country depends almost entirely on external systems to monitor its own rivers, forests, mountains, borders and disasters, it is not merely a technical issue. It is a question of capacity. Who collects the data? Who processes it? Who has access first? Whose priorities shape the system? In a crisis, these questions become urgent.

So far, Nepal has already made some progress. NepaliSat-1, our first satellite, was launched in 2019. Nepal has also engaged with the International Telecommunication Union on orbital and frequency rights, and has been assigned two ‘orbital slots’ that remain part of our underrealised space capacity. This shows that Nepal’s connection to space is real. What we need now is a national decision to take it seriously.

A Nepali space programme need not copy the United States, India, China or Europe. It should not be built around prestige alone. It should be built around public value and around the needs Nepal can actually act on.

This means training students and engineers to use satellite data. It means helping municipalities use mapping to plan for disasters. It means improving access to climate and hazard data for local governments. It means bringing together universities, ministries, private companies and international partners to address practical problems. And it means building a vocabulary of space policy in Nepal, not just celebrating space when some foreign country does something impressive.

In Nepal, we often see imagination as a luxury. We tell young people to be practical. We advise them to leave if necessary. We encourage them to dream, but not here. If you want to pursue advanced science, you leave. If you want to work on the future, you leave. If you want to create something world-class, you leave. This is why symbolism matters.

A future Nepali space mission would not solve all of Nepal’s problems. It should not come before hospitals, roads, jobs or schools. But it could still matter deeply if it is attached to research, education and national capacity. The value would not only be in one person going to space. It would be in what the mission forces us to build around it: Science education, public engagement, international partnerships, research questions and a broader sense of possibility.
