Kisan Dev said his 30-year-old son ran a small plastic sack manufacturing business from their home, which was the family's primary source of income. His death, he said, has left the family without financial support.

Om Prakash is survived by his parents, a younger brother and a married sister. His brother, Manoj Mehta, had been working in Malaysia and returned to Nepal on Tuesday after learning of the incident.

Committee coordinator Bhupendra Thapa said the panel would prepare a detailed report based on evidence collected from the scene, witness accounts and consultations with stakeholders before submitting it to the Home Ministry.

Om Prakash was killed after being struck by a bullet fired by the Armed Police Force during the clashes, according to hospital officials. They said the bullet entered through his left armpit. Although he was rushed to Neuro Hospital in Biratnagar for treatment, doctors declared him dead on arrival.

His body has remained in the hospital morgue for the past three days after the family refused to accept it until their demands are met. As a result, the post-mortem examination has also been delayed.

Deputy Superintendent of Police Chandra Bahadur Khadka, Sunsari Police spokesperson, said authorities remain in regular contact with the family and that the post-mortem would be conducted once an agreement is reached.

Meanwhile, civil society groups organised a peace rally in Itahari on Wednesday, saying the Dewanganj violence had damaged religious and social harmony.

The march, organised by Nagarik Samaj Itahari, began at the city's main intersection, passed through the market area and concluded with a public gathering.

Addressing the rally, former minister Ram Kumar Subba called on all communities to remain committed to preserving religious and social harmony.

articles.title: धर्म र समुदायका नाममा समाज विभाजन गर्ने प्रयास स्वीकार्य छैन : अहबर अन्सारी
articles.summary:
राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी (रास्वपा) का सांसद अहबर अन्सारीले धर्म, जात र समुदायका नाममा समाजलाई विभाजन गर्ने कुनै पनि प्रयास स्वीकार्य नहुने बताएका छन्। बिहीबार प्रतिनिधिसभाको बैठकमा बोल्दै उनले नेपाल ऐतिहासिक रूपमा धार्मिक सहिष्णुता, सामाजिक सद्भाव र विविधताको सम्मान गर्ने देश भएकाले धार्मिक वा जातीय द्वेष फैलाउने गतिविधिप्रति राज्य गम्भीर बन्नुपर्ने बताए।

सांसद अन्सारीले नेपालमा हिन्दु, मुस्लिम, बौद्ध, क्रिश्चियनलगायत विभिन्न धर्म र समुदायका नागरिक आपसी सद्भावका साथ बस्दै आएको उल्लेख गर्दै धार्मिक नाराको दुरुपयोग गरेर एक समुदायलाई अर्को समुदायविरुद्ध उक्साउने गतिविधि तत्काल रोक्न सरकारसँग आग्रह गरे।

उनले विश्वका विभिन्न मुलुकमा समुदायबीच घृणा फैलिँदा मानवअधिकारमाथि असर परेको उदाहरण दिँदै मधेशलाई पनि द्वन्द्व र साम्प्रदायिक तनावतर्फ धकेल्ने प्रयास भइरहेको बताए । राजनीतिक स्वार्थ पूरा गर्न धार्मिक तथा जातीय विभाजनको वातावरण सिर्जना गर्ने व्यक्तिहरूलाई कानुनी दायरामा ल्याउनुपर्ने उनको माग थियो।

सांसद अन्सारीले साम्प्रदायिक हिंसा गोली चलाएर मात्र सुरु नहुने उल्लेख गर्दै घृणात्मक अभिव्यक्ति, सामाजिक सञ्जाल, सञ्चारमाध्यम र सार्वजनिक मञ्चबाट फैलाइने द्वेषपूर्ण प्रचार नै हिंसाको प्रारम्भिक आधार बन्न सक्ने चेतावनी दिए। उनले यस्ता गतिविधिमा संलग्न व्यक्तिहरूको पहिचान गरी कानुनबमोजिम कारबाही गर्न सरकारसँग माग गरे।

रोहिंग्या वा बंगलादेशीको विषयलाई लिएर समाजमा डर, त्रास र भ्रम सिर्जना गर्ने प्रयास पनि स्वीकार्य नहुने उनको भनाइ थियो। उनले यस्ता संवेदनशील विषयमा राज्यले निष्पक्ष, तथ्यमा आधारित र सूक्ष्म अनुसन्धान गरेर मात्रै आवश्यक कदम चाल्नुपर्नेमा जोड दिए।

articles.title: सिरहाको गोलबजारमा कर्फ्यूकै बीच गोली चल्यो : गणेश यादवको मृत्यु, सेना परिचालनपछि अवस्था तनावग्रस्त
articles.summary:
सिरहाको गोलबजारमा कर्फ्यू आदेश जारी रहेका बेला भएको झडपका क्रममा गोली लागेर एक जनाको मृत्यु भएको छ। घटनापछि गोलबजार क्षेत्रको सुरक्षा अवस्था थप संवेदनशील बनेको छ भने स्थानीय प्रशासनले सेना परिचालन गरेको छ।

सिरहाका सहायक प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी चेतराज बरालका अनुसार गोली लागेर मृत्यु हुने व्यक्ति गणेश यादव रहेका छन्। दुई पक्षबीचको विवाद उग्र बन्दै गएपछि झडप भएको र त्यसक्रममा गोली चलेको छ । घटनापछि गोलबजार तथा आसपासका क्षेत्रमा उच्च सुरक्षा सतर्कता अपनाइएको छ। नेपाल प्रहरी, सशस्त्र प्रहरी र नेपाली सेनाको संयुक्त टोली परिचालन गरी स्थिति नियन्त्रणमा लिने प्रयास भइरहेको प्रशासनले जनाएको छ।

प्रशासनले सर्वसाधारणलाई अफवाहको पछि नलाग्न, कर्फ्यू आदेशको पूर्ण पालना गर्न तथा शान्ति–सुरक्षा कायम राख्न सहयोग गर्न आग्रह गरेको छ। घटनाको विस्तृत अनुसन्धान जारी रहेको प्रहरीले जनाएको छ।

articles.title: नेपालमा चर्किएको द्वन्द्वको समाधान बेलैमा खोजौँ
articles.summary:
सुनसरीको देवानगञ्ज–३ कप्तानगञ्जमा भएको हिंसात्मक घटनाले सुरु गरेको तनाव अब केवल एउटा जिल्लाको सुरक्षा चुनौतीमा सीमित देखिएको छैन।

गोलीकाण्डमा घाइते भएका २१ वर्षीय जयप्रकाश मेहताको उपचारका क्रममा मृत्यु भएसँगै मृतकको संख्या दुई पुगेको छ। त्यससँगै विरोध प्रदर्शन, कर्फ्यु, सुरक्षा सतर्कता र राजनीतिक प्रतिक्रियाहरूले संकेत गरेको छ कि नेपाल अहिले सामाजिक सद्भाव र राजनीतिक व्यवस्थापन दुवैको कठिन परीक्षणबाट गुज्रिरहेको छ।

घटनाको प्रभाव सुनसरीबाट धनुषा, सिरहा लगायत मधेसका विभिन्न जिल्लासम्म फैलिएको छ। धनुषामा कर्फ्यु आदेश जारी गरिएको छ भने सिरहाको गोलबजारमा दुई पक्षबीच झडप भएपछि अवस्था तनावपूर्ण बनेको छ। मधेस प्रदेश सरकारले सबै सरकारी कार्यालयलाई अत्यावश्यक कामबाहेक सरकारी सवारी प्रयोग नगर्न निर्देशन दिएको छ, जसले सुरक्षा संवेदनशीलता सामान्य अवस्थाभन्दा निकै बढेको देखाउँछ।

सुनसरीको घटना तत्कालीन झडप वा गोलीकाण्ड मात्र होइन। यसले पछिल्ला केही वर्षदेखि विस्तारै बढ्दै आएको सामाजिक अविश्वास, धार्मिक तथा पहिचानका मुद्दामा बढ्दो ध्रुवीकरण र सामाजिक सञ्जालमार्फत फैलिने उत्तेजक सामग्रीको प्रभावलाई सतहमा ल्याएको छ।

नेपाल परम्परागत रूपमा धार्मिक सहिष्णुताको उदाहरण मानिँदै आएको देश हो। एउटै धार्मिक स्थललाई विभिन्न समुदायले आ–आफ्नो आस्थाअनुसार पूज्ने अभ्यास, साझा पर्वहरूमा विभिन्न समुदायको सहभागिता र मिश्रित सामाजिक संरचनाले नेपाली समाजलाई बलियो बनाएको थियो। तर पछिल्ला वर्षहरूमा यही सहिष्णुतामाथि चुनौती देखिन थालेको छ।

राजनीति किन कमजोर देखियो?

प्रतिनिधिसभामा सम्बोधन गर्दै पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री पुष्पकमल दाहाल ‘प्रचण्ड’ले देशको राजनीतिक अवस्था सहज नरहेको बताएका छन्। उनले जनताले निर्वाचनमार्फत व्यक्त गरेको अपेक्षाअनुसार सरकार सञ्चालन हुन नसकेको र जनतामा निराशा बढ्दै गएको टिप्पणी गरेका छन्।

यो टिप्पणी केवल सरकारको आलोचना मात्र होइन। आर्थिक सुस्तता, रोजगारीको अभाव, महँगी, युवाको बढ्दो पलायन र शासनप्रतिको अविश्वासले समाजमा असन्तुष्टि बढाइरहेको संकेत पनि हो। यस्ता परिस्थितिमा कुनै पनि स्थानीय विवाद छिट्टै ठूलो सामाजिक वा राजनीतिक तनावमा रूपान्तरण हुने जोखिम बढ्छ।

सद्भाव जोगाउने चिन्ता

राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टीका सचेतक प्रकाशचन्द्र परियारले संसद्मा दिएको अभिव्यक्ति अहिलेको परिस्थितिको अर्को महत्वपूर्ण पक्ष उजागर गर्छ। उनले नेपाललाई विविधता र सहिष्णुताको देश भन्दै सामाजिक सद्भाव भड्काउने प्रयासप्रति उच्च सतर्क रहन आग्रह गरेका छन्।

उनको भनाइले उठाउँएको प्रश्न छ:- नेपालमा बाह्य प्रभाव, सामाजिक सञ्जालको दुरुपयोग वा संगठित रूपमा समाजलाई विभाजित गर्ने प्रयास बढ्दै गएको हो? यसको स्पष्ट प्रमाण अनुसन्धानबाट मात्र स्थापित हुन सक्छ। तर पछिल्ला घटनाले यस्ता आशंकामाथि गम्भीर अनुसन्धान र तथ्यमा आधारित निष्कर्ष आवश्यक रहेको देखाएको छ।

सरकारको चुनौती

सुनसरी घटनापछि राष्ट्रिय सुरक्षा परिषद्को बैठक बसेर परिस्थितिको समीक्षा गरिएको छ। आगामी दिनमा सामाजिक सद्भाव कायम राख्न सबै सुरक्षा निकाय र सरोकारवालाबीच समन्वय बढाउने निर्णय गरिएको छ।

तर केवल सुरक्षा परिचालनले मात्र दीर्घकालीन समाधान दिन सक्दैन। हिंसाको कारण निष्पक्ष अनुसन्धान, दोषीमाथि कानुनी कारबाही, अफवाह नियन्त्रण, स्थानीय समुदायबीच संवाद र राजनीतिक नेतृत्वको जिम्मेवार अभिव्यक्ति समान रूपमा आवश्यक छन्।

यदि राज्यले न्यायिक प्रक्रिया कमजोर बनायो वा कुनै पक्षले न्याय नपाएको अनुभूति गर्‍यो भने असन्तुष्टि थप गहिरिन सक्छ।

सामाजिक सञ्जालको प्रभाव

पछिल्ला घटनामा अर्को महत्वपूर्ण पक्ष सामाजिक सञ्जाल बनेको छ। पुष्टि नभएका सूचना, उत्तेजक भिडियो, धार्मिक भावनालाई उक्साउने सामग्री र भ्रामक प्रचारले स्थानीय घटनालाई केही घण्टामै राष्ट्रिय तनावमा बदल्ने क्षमता राख्छ।

यसैले अभिव्यक्ति स्वतन्त्रताको सम्मान गर्दै पनि हिंसा उक्साउने, झुटा सूचना फैलाउने र समुदायबीच घृणा बढाउने गतिविधिमाथि प्रभावकारी निगरानी आवश्यक देखिन्छ।

नेपाल अहिले पूर्ण रूपमा द्वन्द्वग्रस्त अवस्थामा पुगेको निष्कर्ष निकाल्न मिल्दैन। तर पछिल्ला घटनाले सामाजिक सम्बन्ध कमजोर बनाउने संकेत अवश्य दिएका छन्। यदि स्थानीय विवादहरूलाई समयमै समाधान गरिएन, राजनीतिक नेतृत्व जिम्मेवार बनेन, कानुनी कारबाही निष्पक्ष भएन र अफवाह नियन्त्रणमा प्रभावकारी काम भएन भने यस्ता घटनाले व्यापक सामाजिक विभाजन निम्त्याउने जोखिम रहन्छ।

नेपालको सबैभन्दा ठूलो शक्ति यसको विविधता, सहिष्णुता र सहअस्तित्वको संस्कृति हो। यही आधारलाई कमजोर पार्ने कुनै पनि गतिविधि केवल सुरक्षा चुनौती होइन, राष्ट्रिय एकतामाथिको चुनौती पनि हो। त्यसैले अहिलेको आवश्यकता बल प्रयोगभन्दा बढी न्याय, संवाद, पारदर्शिता र विश्वास पुनःस्थापनाको हो।

सुनसरीबाट सुरु भएको तनावले राज्य, राजनीतिक दल, सुरक्षा निकाय र नागरिक समाज सबैलाई सामाजिक सद्भावको रक्षा केवल नाराले होइन, समयमै गरिने निष्पक्ष निर्णय, जिम्मेवार राजनीति र नागरिकको संयमित व्यवहारबाट मात्र सम्भव हुन्छ भन्ने सन्देश दिएको छ।

articles.title: मधेस प्रदेशका सबै जिल्लामा सरकारी सवारी साधन सञ्चालनमा कडाइ
articles.summary:
मधेस प्रदेश सरकारले प्रदेशभर बढ्दो सुरक्षा संवेदनशीलतालाई मध्यनजर गर्दै सबै जिल्लामा सरकारी सवारी साधनको प्रयोगमा कडाइ गरेको छ।

गृह, सञ्चार तथा कानुन मन्त्रालयले प्रदेशअन्तर्गतका सबै सरकारी कार्यालयलाई पत्राचार गर्दै अत्यावश्यक सरकारी कामबाहेक अन्य कुनै पनि प्रयोजनका लागि सरकारी सवारी साधन प्रयोग नगर्न निर्देशन दिएको हो।

मन्त्रालयका अधिकृत राधेशंकर प्रसाद पन्तद्वारा जारी पत्रमा हालको सुरक्षा अवस्थालाई दृष्टिगत गर्दै सरकारी सवारी साधनको सुरक्षित व्यवस्थापन गर्न तथा अनावश्यक रूपमा सञ्चालन नगर्न आग्रह गरिएको छ।

पत्रमा भनिएको छ, ‘कार्यालय प्रयोजनका लागि उपलब्ध सरकारी सवारी साधनहरूको हालको सुरक्षा संवेदनशीलतालाई दृष्टिगत गरी अत्यावश्यक सरकारी कामबाहेक अन्य प्रयोजनमा प्रयोग नगर्नरनगराउन तथा सवारी साधनको सुरक्षित व्यवस्थापन गराउन आदेशानुसार अनुरोध छ।’

पछिल्ला दिनहरूमा मधेश प्रदेशका केही जिल्लामा उत्पन्न तनावपूर्ण अवस्थाका कारण सुरक्षा निकाय उच्च सतर्कतामा रहेका बेला प्रदेश सरकारले सरकारी सम्पत्ति र कर्मचारीको सुरक्षालाई प्राथमिकतामा राख्दै यस्तो निर्देशन जारी गरेको हो।

articles.title: धर्म र समुदायका नाममा समाज विभाजन गर्ने प्रयास स्वीकार्य छैन : अहबर अन्सारी
articles.summary:
राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी (रास्वपा) का सांसद अहबर अन्सारीले धर्म, जात र समुदायका नाममा समाजलाई विभाजन गर्ने कुनै पनि प्रयास स्वीकार्य नहुने बताएका छन्। बिहीबार प्रतिनिधिसभाको बैठकमा बोल्दै उनले नेपाल ऐतिहासिक रूपमा धार्मिक सहिष्णुता, सामाजिक सद्भाव र विविधताको सम्मान गर्ने देश भएकाले धार्मिक वा जातीय द्वेष फैलाउने गतिविधिप्रति राज्य गम्भीर बन्नुपर्ने बताए।

सांसद अन्सारीले नेपालमा हिन्दु, मुस्लिम, बौद्ध, क्रिश्चियनलगायत विभिन्न धर्म र समुदायका नागरिक आपसी सद्भावका साथ बस्दै आएको उल्लेख गर्दै धार्मिक नाराको दुरुपयोग गरेर एक समुदायलाई अर्को समुदायविरुद्ध उक्साउने गतिविधि तत्काल रोक्न सरकारसँग आग्रह गरे।

उनले विश्वका विभिन्न मुलुकमा समुदायबीच घृणा फैलिँदा मानवअधिकारमाथि असर परेको उदाहरण दिँदै मधेशलाई पनि द्वन्द्व र साम्प्रदायिक तनावतर्फ धकेल्ने प्रयास भइरहेको बताए । राजनीतिक स्वार्थ पूरा गर्न धार्मिक तथा जातीय विभाजनको वातावरण सिर्जना गर्ने व्यक्तिहरूलाई कानुनी दायरामा ल्याउनुपर्ने उनको माग थियो।

सांसद अन्सारीले साम्प्रदायिक हिंसा गोली चलाएर मात्र सुरु नहुने उल्लेख गर्दै घृणात्मक अभिव्यक्ति, सामाजिक सञ्जाल, सञ्चारमाध्यम र सार्वजनिक मञ्चबाट फैलाइने द्वेषपूर्ण प्रचार नै हिंसाको प्रारम्भिक आधार बन्न सक्ने चेतावनी दिए। उनले यस्ता गतिविधिमा संलग्न व्यक्तिहरूको पहिचान गरी कानुनबमोजिम कारबाही गर्न सरकारसँग माग गरे।

रोहिंग्या वा बंगलादेशीको विषयलाई लिएर समाजमा डर, त्रास र भ्रम सिर्जना गर्ने प्रयास पनि स्वीकार्य नहुने उनको भनाइ थियो। उनले यस्ता संवेदनशील विषयमा राज्यले निष्पक्ष, तथ्यमा आधारित र सूक्ष्म अनुसन्धान गरेर मात्रै आवश्यक कदम चाल्नुपर्नेमा जोड दिए।

articles.title: Nepal’s health worker shortage is driving doctor-patient conflict
articles.summary:
On Wednesday, a doctor serving at a primary health care centre in Dolpa district called Dr Bishwa Raj Dawadi, general secretary of the Nepal Medical Association, with a dilemma. As the association urged doctors to boycott services after a colleague was assaulted in Birgunj, he wanted to know whether he too should join the protest.

The doctor explained that he was the only physician at the facility, responsible for the outpatient department, inpatient ward and emergency services.

"I could not ask him to stop providing services in support of the association's protest against the assault on fellow doctors," Dawadi said. "As human beings, we also have a moral responsibility towards our patients. If we continue the protest in its most extreme form by boycotting services, it could lead to unfortunate consequences."

The predicament is not unique. Most of Nepal’s 187 primary health care centres have only one doctor and many of them are contract employees or scholarship doctors deployed by the Ministry of Health. They are expected to provide round-the-clock service to patients.

Successive governments’ failure to address chronic shortages of health workers has left doctors overstretched, patients underserved, and relations between the two increasingly strained.

“The problem is not with patients, and patients should not have problems with doctors either,” said Dr Sanjeev Tiwari, senior vice president of the association. “The government’s failure to recruit enough health workers is the root cause of the growing conflict between doctors and patients. It is turning them into sworn enemies, which is not good for society.”

Doctors say whether it is daytime or the middle of the night, a lone doctor at a primary health care facility is expected to be available whenever patients arrive. Even when doctors have personal health problems or family emergencies, they are expected to remain on duty.

Doctors say such chronic understaffing lies at the heart of the growing friction between health workers and patients.

“Like many other doctors, I also worked under the same circumstances,” said Dawadi. “Whenever I felt exhausted or burned out, I would take leave and go home to rest.”

Even in such a situation, the government does not send a replacement, and patients are deprived of basic health care services. Aggression of the relatives of patients often grows when they cannot find a doctor.

In the recent case at Narayani Hospital, Birgunj, a doctor on duty in the emergency department was assaulted following the death of a 45-year-old heart patient, who suffered a massive heart attack. Doctors said the hospital lacked the trained human resources needed to handle such critical cases. Enraged relatives attacked Dr Pramod Ram, leaving him injured and bleeding.

The injured doctor, who was admitted to the National Trauma Centre in Kathmandu, told office-bearers of the association that verbal abuse of health workers and doctors in hospital emergency departments had become routine, with such incidents occurring almost every day.

“We stopped caring about verbal abuse and threats long ago, but this time they hit me and broke my head,” Dawadi quoted Dr Ram as saying.

Multiple doctors the Post spoke to say that the government’s longstanding failure to recruit doctors and health workers is the main reason for the rising conflict between doctors and patients.

The government has not increased permanent doctor posts for 34 years. At the time when the organisational structure of state-run health facilities was approved in 1991, the country’s population was 18.4 million. According to the 2021 national census, the population has grown to 29.1 million.

There are around 1,500 permanent doctor posts under the three tiers of government—federal, provincial and local. Some also take leave, some take unpaid leave, and the Health Ministry itself sends some of them abroad for further studies.

“Around 1,500 additional doctors, including those hired on contract and scholarship doctors, are serving across the country,” said Dr Samir Kumar Adhikari, joint spokesperson at the Ministry of Health and Food Safety. “This year, the new government has approved 977 new permanent doctor posts, but it will take time for the Public Service Commission to recruit them.”

Experts say that, along with health posts and primary health care centres, most provincial and federal-level hospitals have been facing a severe crunch of human resources for years.

“We cannot ensure universal health coverage to all and retain trained doctors in the country unless we create permanent positions," said Dr Roshan Pokhrel, former health secretary. “Multiple services have increased and expanded, but human resources have not increased accordingly. It will be difficult to continue services in the long run if the underlying problems are ignored.”

The World Health Organisation Global Strategy on Human Resources for Health states that countries need at least 4.45 doctors, nurses and midwives per 1,000 people to achieve universal health coverage. Nepal’s health workforce remains below this benchmark.

Meanwhile, officials at the Nepal Medical Association said that they received reports of vandalism of the intensive care unit of a Bhaktapur-based hospital on Wednesday evening, while agitating doctors and the government representatives were signing an agreement to resume services and for the government to address their safety concerns.

articles.title: Nepal-India boundary talks in Lucknow on August 12-14
articles.summary:
At a time when the boundary issue with India has become one of the most discussed topics in Nepal, the two countries are set to sit next month to discuss technical aspects of the border.

The 13th meeting of the Survey Officials' Committee (SOC) is scheduled to be held in Lucknow from August 12 to 14, according to a senior official at Nepal's Department of Survey. The meeting is expected to approve the plan and budget for implementing the agreement reached at the seventh meeting of the Boundary Working Group (BWG), the highest bilateral technical mechanism dealing with boundary issues, excluding the disputes over Susta and Kalapani. The BWG met on July 30 last year. The SOC is also not mandated to discuss Susta and Kalapani disputes.

Sushil Dangol, deputy director general of the Department of Survey, will lead the Nepali delegation.

The BWG had agreed to complete technical boundary work—including construction of new boundary pillars and the repair of damaged ones jointly—within three years. At last year's meeting, the two sides also agreed to prepare an inventory of encroachments of the no-man's land and document cross-border property holdings by citizens of both countries.

"We have already completed two years of the agreed timeline. The upcoming meeting will chart out the plan for the remaining one year," the official said.

The boundary issue has remained a key agenda between Nepal and India since Nepal issued its new political map in 2020. However, bilateral efforts to resolve technical boundary issues date back much earlier, particularly to Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's state visit to Nepal in 2014.

The agreement to establish the BWG was reached during that visit with the mandate to clear the no-man's land, construct, restore and repair boundary pillars, update records of cross-border property holdings, and undertake other technical tasks related to border management.

In 2015, both sides set a three-year deadline to complete the technical work. When that target was missed, they renewed the deadline in 2017, aiming to complete the work by 2022. However, both deadlines lapsed due to a combination of factors, including funding constraints, the Covid pandemic, recurring boundary disputes and adverse climatic conditions.

"Once the agenda is finalised and shared between the two sides, there will be greater clarity on the issues to be discussed," a government official said.

The Covid pandemic and the strain in bilateral ties following the 2020 boundary dispute also delayed BWG meetings, leaving the mechanism inactive for six years after its last meeting in 2019.

Officials at the Department of Survey say the upcoming meeting is also expected to review the upgrading of Global Positioning System (GPS) base stations. Nepal and India currently use the internationally accepted Nepal-India Boundary Global Navigation Satellite System (NIB GNSS) to map boundary pillars.

The latest boundary maps—excluding the disputed areas of Kalapani and Susta—were prepared using GPS technology under an agreement reached in 2007. Based on the resulting 182 map sheets, the BWG has been tasked with constructing new boundary pillars where they are missing, repairing damaged pillars, clearing the no-man's land and preparing an inventory of cross-border property holdings.

Apart from the BWG and the SOC, the two countries also operate Joint Field Survey Teams (FSTs). Together, these three mechanisms are responsible for constructing, restoring and repairing boundary pillars, clearing the no-man's land, conducting GPS-based mapping, collecting data on cross-border property holdings and addressing other technical boundary issues.

According to the Department of Survey, a total of 8,554 boundary pillars have been installed along the Nepal-India border. Of these, 1,325 are missing, while 1,956 are either partially or completely damaged. Under the BWG framework, the Survey Officials' Committee and the Joint Field Survey Teams provide technical expertise and carry out field-level implementation.

The FSTs are using updated technical modalities to inspect, repair and maintain boundary pillars. They have also agreed on the need to adopt newer surveying and mapping technologies to improve the efficiency of the BWG and its supporting mechanisms, another Department of Survey official said.

Nepal and India share a 1,880-kilometre border spanning 27 districts. Before the Covid pandemic, technical boundary work had been completed in Jhapa, Sunsari, Kailali and Parsa districts.

The immediate priority of the BWG is to prepare a comprehensive blueprint for completing the remaining boundary work. This includes documenting cross-border property holdings, repairing or reinstalling damaged and missing boundary pillars, upgrading GPS infrastructure, and addressing technical issues arising from rivers that have changed course over the years.

Some boundary pillars have already been jointly repaired by Nepal's Armed Police Force (APF) and India's Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB), and data from those works has been forwarded to the Survey Officials' Committee. Officials say fresh field data will also be reviewed to identify additional pillars that need to be installed, repaired or maintained.

Over the decades, changes in the courses of hundreds of rivers have shifted thousands of hectares of land to either side of the border. The Survey Officials' Committee and the Joint Field Survey Teams are currently documenting these changes, which will provide the technical basis for future decisions by the two governments.

articles.title: University Grants Commission yet to issue equivalence certificates after taking over role from TU
articles.summary:
On Wednesday morning, Pramod Sah arrived at the University Grants Commission office in Sanothimi, Bhaktapur, carrying a bag of documents. He had hoped to return with an equivalency certificate for his MD (postgraduate) degree, which he earned from a university in Chandigarh, India.

However, despite spending the entire day making rounds of the office, he did not receive the certificate he was seeking. Instead, he was told that he would have to wait a little longer.

“The UGC officials asked me to wait until the necessary legal procedures are completed and staff arrangements made,” Sah said.

The UGC advised him to submit an online application and wait for the time being. Sah, who is originally from Biratnagar, has recently been living in India.

“I came to Nepal specifically for this work, but nothing happened,” he said.

Like Sah, 26-year-old Bishal Bhujel, who completed his optometry studies in Bengaluru, faced a similar problem. Since an equivalency certificate is required to participate in Nepal’s licensing examination, he had gone to the UGC. However, instead of a permanent certificate, he was provided only with a temporary letter.

“Our licensing exam applications are opening soon. They prepared a temporary document so that we could take the exam,” he said. “They told us to return later for the permanent certificate because the regulations and other procedures have not yet been completed.”

Although Bhujel hopes the temporary letter will fulfil his immediate need, it is not a permanent solution. As a result, many students who have returned after completing their studies abroad are currently uncertain about their future.

More than a week has passed since the service began after the responsibility for issuing equivalency certificates for academic qualifications was transferred from the Tribhuvan University to the commission. However, not a single permanent equivalency certificate has been issued so far.

The commission started accepting applications on July 22, and more than 1,000 students have applied for equivalency certificates so far. According to the commission, around 200 students visit daily to apply for equivalency. However, no student has yet received a permanent certificate, leaving them uncertain about further studies, licensing examinations, and other academic procedures.

An equivalency certificate is mandatory for recognition of academic degrees obtained from foreign universities in Nepal. Based on this certificate, students can pursue further studies at Nepali universities, apply for scholarships, and participate in professional activities. Students in health-related fields have been particularly affected by the UGC’s delays. Those returning after studying medicine, physiotherapy, optometry, and other health sciences abroad require equivalency certificates to complete licensing procedures.

After amendments were made to the University Grants Commission Act in August last year, the authority to issue equivalency certificates, previously handled by the Tribhuvan University for decades, was transferred to the commission. Under this arrangement, the commission announced that it would begin providing equivalency services from July 22.

However, even a year after the transfer of responsibility, the commission has not been able to fully establish the required structures and decision-making procedures, causing difficulties for students.

The main reason for the delay is that the necessary regulations have not been issued even a year after the Act was amended. Although the regulations must be approved by the Council of Ministers based on a proposal from the Ministry of Education, the process has not moved forward.

Dularaj Chimariya, deputy director at the commission, said delays in issuing the regulations were caused by insufficient administrative preparation, a lack of leadership, and other procedural issues.

“Currently, the commission does not have a chairperson, secretary, or board members. The secretary is supposed to coordinate the equivalency determination committee. The decision-making process has been affected by the absence of a secretary,” he said.

Chimariya said that once the regulations are approved and the board is formed, the process of issuing equivalency certificates will operate normally.

According to him, an online system has been introduced to eliminate the need for students to repeatedly visit the office for equivalency certificates. Once online applications are received, the approval process will begin, and the foreign degree holders will receive notifications for updates. After the documents are verified, students will be informed to pay the required fee. Once all procedures are completed, they will be notified that the certificate is ready and will be able to print it online.

However, when this system will be fully implemented depends on when the regulations are issued and when the board is formed.

Under the temporary arrangement, students with urgent needs are being provided temporary letters, but these have not been able to replace permanent equivalency certificates. According to commission data, only around 40 students have so far received temporary letters stating that their equivalency process is ongoing.

Sajina Koju, who completed her physiotherapy studies at Shree Devi College in Bangalore, has also received a similar temporary letter.

“I do not know whether it will actually work,” she said. “Now we have to come back again later for the same work.”

articles.title: Saudi Arabia halts visas for Nepali workers needing skill certificates after Nepal seals testing centre
articles.summary:
Saudi Arabia has stopped issuing work visas to Nepali workers in five job categories that require mandatory skill verification certificates after Nepal’s government sealed the Kathmandu-based institute conducting the tests.

The Saudi Arabian embassy suspended visa processing for workers requiring Skill Verification Programme (SVP) certification after authorities sealed the Industrial Training Institute in Basundhara last Wednesday, saying the centre did not have legal authorisation to conduct skill assessments.

The shutdown has created uncertainty for thousands of Nepali migrant workers seeking jobs in Saudi Arabia, one of Nepal’s largest labour destinations.

Mahesh Kumar Basnet, senior vice-president of the Nepal Association of Foreign Employment Agencies, said visas were still being issued for workers in jobs that do not require SVP certification.

“We have asked recruitment agencies not to submit visa applications for jobs where Saudi Arabia has made skill verification certificates mandatory,” Basnet told Kantipur after meeting Saudi diplomatic officials on Tuesday. “A private institution has created a monopoly in the name of skill testing, piling financial burden on workers. This is unacceptable.”

Saudi Arabia has required skill verification certificates for Nepali workers going for jobs such as loading and unloading goods, portering, cart operation and construction work.

Workers are required to pay a $50 examination fee, equivalent to around Rs7,500. However, there is no legal provision allowing workers or recruitment agencies to directly pay the fee. Instead, Sai Vision Pvt Ltd has been collecting Rs10,000, including service charges, for arranging the process.

A $50 charge has been for recognition of prior learning (RPL), but the details of how the RPL system will work remain unclear.

The Ministry of Youth, Labour and Employment said it was holding discussions with Saudi authorities to resolve the dispute.

“The labour minister has been in talks with the Saudi ambassador,” said Pitambar Ghimire, spokesperson for the ministry. “A diplomatic note has also been sent.”

Saudi officials have expressed concern that Nepal has effectively suspended the SVP programme. Nepal’s labour officials, however, say the programme itself has not been stopped. They argue that the institute conducting the assessments did not have the authority to do so.

Nepal says skill testing should be conducted through a mutually agreed mechanism that protects workers’ interests.

“The process should be based on a bilateral agreement. Skill tests should be limited to occupations where workers’ abilities can be properly assessed, rather than being imposed on ordinary labourers. The government must also ensure that workers are not forced to bear the cost,” a labour ministry official said.

A labour agreement signed between Nepal and Saudi Arabia in January states that recruitment-related issues will be decided by a joint technical committee between the two countries. However, no bilateral agreement has been reached on introducing a skill certification programme.

Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development says the SVP was introduced to verify professional qualifications before issuing employment visas.

Saudi Arabia received around 77,000 Nepali workers last year. Of them, 67 percent went on general labour visas, eight percent worked in the service sector and 12 percent went as drivers and machine operators.

Foreign employment agencies say experiences from India and Bangladesh show that workers ultimately bear the cost of such certification schemes.

“The testing fee is one burden. If workers fail, they have to repeat the process and this adds to the cost,” said Dik Bahadur Khatri, president of the Nepal Association of Foreign Employment Agencies.

Saudi Arabia had planned to implement the SVP system from June 17. The rollout was delayed after foreign employment agencies vandalised the training centre assigned to conduct the assessments.

According to a notice issued by the Saudi Embassy in Kathmandu, workers must first register online through Saudi Arabia’s Professional Accreditation Portal before taking the skill test. They must then pay the fee in US dollars.

Applicants must select their occupation from the list of eligible professions, choose an approved testing centre and pick an available examination date. The test lasts three hours, with results expected within 24 hours to one week.

Saudi Arabia allows workers up to three attempts to pass the assessment. Those who fail after three attempts become ineligible to travel to the kingdom for employment.

Saudi authorities have said the programme is being introduced across all labour source countries.

articles.title: पार्टी सदस्यलाई रेडक्रसमा निषेध
articles.summary:
नेपाल रेडक्रस सोसाइटी जिल्ला शाखा भक्तपुरले सक्रिय राजनीतिमा संलग्न व्यक्तिलाई रेडक्रसको सदस्यता तथा नेतृत्वमा स्थान नदिने नीति सार्वजनिक गरेपछि यसको पक्ष–विपक्षमा बहस सुरु भएको छ।

नवनियुक्त जिल्ला सभापति रामेश्वर थापाले पदभार ग्रहण गर्दै रेडक्रसलाई राजनीतिक प्रभावबाट मुक्त राख्ने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरे। उनले अबदेखि विशुद्ध समाजसेवामा समर्पित र कुनै राजनीतिक दलको सदस्यता नलिएका व्यक्तिका लागि सदस्यता खुला गरिने बताए।

‘यसअघि सदस्य बन्न राजनीतिक पहुँच वा दलगत सिफारिस आवश्यक पर्ने अवस्था थियो। अब रेडक्रसमा राजनीति हुन दिइँदैन,’ उनले भने। उनका अनुसार स्वतन्त्र नागरिकका लागि शाखा कार्यालयमै खुला सदस्यता डेस्क सञ्चालन गरिनेछ।

रेडक्रसका जानकारहरूका अनुसार विगतमा सदस्यता वितरण र नेतृत्व चयनमा राजनीतिक प्रभाव देखिने गरेको थियो, जसका कारण संस्थाको निष्पक्षता र विश्वसनीयतामाथि प्रश्न उठ्ने गरेको थियो।

थापाले नेपाल रेडक्रस सोसाइटीको विधान २०२० (अठारौँ संशोधन–२०८२) को दफा ७२(३) अनुसार राजनीतिक दल वा भ्रातृ संगठनका पदाधिकारी तथा राजनीतिक दलबाट राज्यका शासकीय संरचनामा रहेका व्यक्तिहरू रेडक्रसका कुनै पनि तहका समिति, आयोग वा उपसमितिमा सदस्य वा पदाधिकारी बन्न नपाउने व्यवस्था रहेको बताए। दोहोरो भूमिकामा रहेका व्यक्तिलाई रेडक्रसबाट अलग हुन पनि आग्रह गरिएको उनले जानकारी दिए।

रेडक्रसका सात आधारभूत सिद्धान्त—मानवता, निष्पक्षता, तटस्थता, स्वतन्त्रता, स्वेच्छिक सेवा, एकता र विश्वव्यापिता—प्रति प्रतिबद्ध जोसुकै नेपाली नागरिकले निर्धारित प्रक्रिया पूरा गरेर सदस्यता लिन सक्ने व्यवस्था रहेको पनि उनले स्पष्ट पारे।

निर्णयपछि मिश्रित प्रतिक्रिया

भक्तपुर शाखाको घोषणापछि सामाजिक सञ्जालमा भने मिश्रित प्रतिक्रिया देखिएको छ। कतिपयले निर्णयको स्वागत गर्दै रेडक्रसको तटस्थता कायम गर्न आवश्यक कदम भनेका छन् भने केहीले मनोनित पदाधिकारीहरूको राजनीतिक पृष्ठभूमिमाथि प्रश्न उठाएका छन्।

नेपाल रेडक्रस सोसाइटी मध्यपुर थिमि शाखाका पूर्वसभापति बाबुकाजी श्रेष्ठले रेडक्रसमा झन् ठूलो राजनीति सुरु भएको टिप्पणी गरेका छन्। उनले रेडक्रसजस्तो मानवीय संस्थालाई राजनीतिक प्रभावबाट पूर्ण रूपमा मुक्त गर्नुपर्ने आवश्यकता औंल्याएका छन्।

यता मानवीय सेवाका क्षेत्रमा कार्यरत व्यक्तिहरू भने यो व्यवस्थाले रेडक्रसप्रति सर्वसाधारणको विश्वास अझ बलियो हुने अपेक्षा व्यक्त गर्छन्। उनीहरूका अनुसार विपद् व्यवस्थापन, रक्तसञ्चार, उद्धार, राहत र स्वास्थ्य सेवामा सक्रिय रेडक्रसको नेतृत्व राजनीतिक प्रभावभन्दा माथि रहनु आवश्यक छ।

नेपाल रेडक्रस सोसाइटी भक्तपुरमा यसअघिको सम्पूर्ण पदाधिकारी समिति विघटन गरी केन्द्रले रामेश्वर थापाको नेतृत्वमा नयाँ समिति मनोनयन गरेको छ। नवनियुक्त पदाधिकारीहरूको पदस्थापन तथा शपथग्रहण कार्यक्रम बिहीबार भक्तपुरमा सम्पन्न भएको थियो।

articles.title: गोलबजार गोलीकाण्ड छानबिन गर्न एसपी रिजालको नेतृत्वमा समिति गठन
articles.summary:
सिरहाको गोलबजारमा भएको घटनाको छानबिन गर्न मधेस प्रदेश प्रहरी कार्यालयले तीन सदस्यीय समिति गठन गरेको छ।

बिहीबार दिउँसो गोलबजारमा गोली लागेर स्थानीय गणेश यादवको मृत्यु भएपछि घटनाको वास्तविकता पत्ता लगाउन प्रहरी कार्यालयले छानबिन समिति बनाएको हो।

समितिको नेतृत्व मधेस प्रदेश प्रहरी कार्यालयका प्रहरी उपरीक्षक (एसपी) भेषराज रिजालले गरेका छन्। समितिमा प्रहरी निरीक्षक (इन्सपेक्टर) यज्ञराज भट्ट र प्रहरी सहायक निरीक्षक (असई) गोविन्द झा सदस्य रहेका छन्।

समितिले घटनाको कारण, संलग्न पक्ष र प्रहरीको भूमिकालगायत विषयमा अध्ययन गरी प्रतिवेदन बुझाउने जनाइएको छ।

articles.title: साढे ३ किमि सडक बनाउन १० वर्ष!
articles.summary:
बुटवलको मुख्य बजार क्षेत्र हुँदै जाने सिद्धार्थ राजमार्गअन्तर्गत राजमार्ग चौराहदेखि गोलपार्कसम्मको साढे ३ किलोमिटर सडक विस्तार सुरु भएको एक दशक बितिसक्दा पनि निर्माण सम्पन्न हुन सकेको छैन। दुईपटक ठेक्का सम्झौता, सातपटक म्याद थप र लागत वृद्धि हुँदासमेत आयोजनाको भौतिक प्रगति करिब ६२ प्रतिशत मात्रै पुगेको छ।

यो सडक २०७३ चैतमा कञ्चनजंघा–बिरुवा जेभीसँग २०७६ भित्र सम्पन्न गर्ने लक्ष्यसहित ५३ करोड ९७ लाख ९९ हजार रुपैयाँमा ठेक्का सम्झौता गरिएको थियो। प्रारम्भिक लागत अनुमान करिब ५६ करोड रुपैयाँ रहेकामा अहिले लागत बढेर ६२ करोड रुपैयाँ पुगेको छ।

तर सडक क्षेत्रभित्रका संरचना हटाउने विषयमा भएको विवाद, केही व्यापारीको अवरोध तथा निर्माण कम्पनीको सुस्त कार्यसम्पादनका कारण आयोजना वर्षौंसम्म अलपत्र पर्‍यो। अदालतले सडक विस्तारको पक्षमा फैसला गरेपछि पनि निर्माणले गति लिन नसकेपछि २०८१ वैशाखमा पहिलो ठेक्का रद्द गरिएको थियो।

त्यसपछि २०८१ असोज १८ गते बबुल दर्शन–मालिका जेभीसँग ३४ करोड ८६ लाख रुपैयाँमा नयाँ ठेक्का सम्झौता भयो। २०८२ असोजभित्र काम सक्ने लक्ष्य राखिएको उक्त कम्पनीका सञ्चालक रुपन्देही–५ बाट निर्वाचित प्रतिनिधिसभा सदस्य तौफिक अहमद खान हुन्।

तर दोस्रो ठेक्कामा पनि निर्माण कार्य समयमै पूरा हुन नसकेपछि पटक–पटक म्याद थप गरिएको छ। पहिलो पटक २०८२ चैतसम्म, त्यसपछि २०८३ असार मसान्तसम्म र अहिले तेस्रोपटक २०८३ असोज २० गतेसम्म म्याद थप गरिएको सडक डिभिजन कार्यालय बुटवलले जनाएको छ।

सडक डिभिजन कार्यालयकी सूचना अधिकारी इन्जिनियर प्रज्ञा शर्माका अनुसार हालसम्म निर्माण कम्पनीलाई १८ करोड ७७ लाख रुपैयाँ भुक्तानी भइसकेको छ। निर्माण कम्पनीले थपिएको अवधिभित्र जसरी पनि काम सम्पन्न गर्ने प्रतिबद्धता जनाएको भन्दै अन्तिमपटक करिब दुई महिना २० दिनको समय थप गरिएको उनले बताइन्।

कार्यालयका अनुसार मुख्य सडकको दुवैतर्फ गरी ६ किलोमिटरमध्ये करिब ४ किलोमिटर कालोपत्रे सम्पन्न भएको छ। सर्भिस लेनतर्फ ४.४ किलोमिटर कालोपत्रे भएको छ भने फुटपाथमा करिब ३ किलोमिटर कालोपत्रे गरिएको छ। २४० वटा स्ट्रिट लाइटमध्ये १८८ वटाको फाउन्डेसन तयार भएको छ भने करिब डेढ किलोमिटर रेलिङ जडान गरिएको छ।

यद्यपि, अबको करिब ६५ दिनभित्र मुख्य सडकको बाँकी करिब २ किलोमिटर, सर्भिस लेन, फुटपाथ, रेलिङ, स्ट्रिट लाइट तथा अन्य फिनिसिङका सबै काम सम्पन्न गर्नुपर्ने अवस्था छ। तर हालको निर्माण गति हेर्दा तोकिएको समयमै काम सकिनेमा स्थानीयवासीले शंका व्यक्त गरेका छन्।

सूचना अधिकारी शर्मा भने वर्षायाम, बिटुमिनको अभावलगायत कारण केही ढिलाइ भए पनि निर्माण कम्पनीले रातदिन काम गरेर असोजभित्र आयोजना सम्पन्न गर्ने प्रतिबद्धता जनाएको बताउँछिन्।

सिद्धार्थ राजमार्गअन्तर्गत बुटवलदेखि बेलहिया नाकासम्मको २७.५ किलोमिटर सडक आर्थिक वर्ष २०६८/६९ देखि व्यापारिक मार्ग परियोजनाअन्तर्गत ६ लेनमा विस्तार गर्न थालिएको हो। अधिकांश खण्ड सम्पन्न भए पनि बुटवल–गोलपार्कको साढे ३ किलोमिटर र बेलहिया नजिकको करिब ६ सय मिटर सडक अझै निर्माणाधीन छन्।

articles.title: डाक्टरको लापरबाहीले सुत्केरीको मृत्यु भएको भन्दै आफन्तद्वारा कपिलवस्तु अस्पतालमा प्रदर्शन
articles.summary:
कपिलवस्तु अस्पतालका डाक्टरहरूको लापरबाहीले कपिलवस्तु नगरपालिका–७ धमौलीकी सुत्केरीको मृत्यु भएको भन्दै मृतक परिवार र स्थानीयवासीले अस्पताल र प्रशासन कार्यालय अगाडि विरोध प्रदर्शन गरेका छन्।

३० वर्षीया चनरमती यादवको शल्यक्रिया गरी गत साउन ७ गते अस्पतालमा सकुशल बच्चा जन्माइएको थियो। सुत्केरी महिलालाई पिसाब फेर्न समस्या आएपछि अस्पतालले डाक्टरहरूको सल्लाहअनुसार थप उपचारका लागि भैरहवास्थित मेडिकल कलेज पठाएको थियो। त्यहाँ उनको चार दिनसम्म उपचार भएको थियो।

उपचारका क्रममा मिर्गौलामा समस्या देखिएपछि दुई पटक श्रीमतीको डायलासिस गरिएको मृतकका श्रीमान् राजेश यादवले बताए। साउन १२ गते श्रीमतीको मृत्यु भएको उनले जानकारी दिए।

श्रीमतीको उपचारमा कपिलवस्तु अस्पतालका डाक्टरले लापरबाही गरेका कारण यस्तो समस्या आएको र अनाहकमा श्रीमतीले ज्यान गुमाउनु परेको उनले आरोप लगाए। आफ्ना तीनवटै सन्तान सामान्य अवस्थामा नै जन्मिएको तर यसपटक भने डाक्टरको लापरबाही देखिएको उनको भनाइ छ।

श्रीमतीको उपचारका क्रममा कपिलवस्तु अस्पतालका स्वास्थ्यकर्मीले दुर्व्यवहारसमेत गरेको उनले गुनासो गरे।

मृतकको शव एम्बुलेन्समै राखेर अस्पताल र प्रशासन कार्यालयमा विरोध प्रदर्शन गरिएको थियो। प्रदर्शनकारीले दोषीलाई कारबाही र मृतक परिवारलाई उचित क्षतिपूर्तिको माग गरेका छन्। उनीहरूले डाक्टरविरुद्ध नाराबाजीसमेत गरेका थिए।

कपिलवस्तु अस्पतालका मेडिकल सुपरिटेन्डेन्ट किशोर बन्जाडेले मृतक महिलाको शल्यक्रियापछि पनि अवस्था सामान्य रहेको र पिसाब फेर्न समस्या आएपछि थप उपचारका लागि रिफर गरिएको बताए।

मेडिकल कलेजमा समेत चार दिनसम्म उपचार भएको र मिर्गौलामै समस्या देखिएपछि महिलाको दुःखद निधन भएको जानकारी आफूलाई त्यहाँका डाक्टरहरूले सम्पर्कका क्रममा दिएको उनले बताए। उनले डाक्टरहरूको कुनै लापरबाही नभएको दाबी गर्दै पोस्टमार्टम रिपोर्ट आएपछि त्यसअनुसार थप कदम चालिने बताए।

मृतक महिलाको शव लुम्बिनी प्रादेशिक अस्पतालमा पोस्टमार्टमका लागि राखिएको थियो। तीन दिनसम्म शवको पोस्टमार्टम हुन सकेको थिएन। बिहीबार बिहान मात्रै पोस्टमार्टम गरिएको थियो।

मृतक परिवार र प्रशासन कार्यालयबीच घटनाका विषयमा छलफलसमेत भएको थियो। सोही क्रममा मृतकका श्रीमान् राजेश कुमार यादवले दोषीमाथि कारबाहीका लागि प्रशासन कार्यालयमार्फत मेडिकल काउन्सिलमा उजुरी दिएका छन्।

उक्त उजुरी मेडिकल काउन्सिलमा पठाइएको सहायक प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी भविश्वर घिमिरेले बताए। उनले मृतकका श्रीमान्लाई कपिलवस्तु अस्पतालमा रोजगारीका लागि प्राथमिकता दिने विषयमा समेत सहमति भएको जानकारी दिए।

काउन्सिलले छानबिन गरी प्रतिवेदन दिएपछि त्यसका आधारमा कारबाही प्रक्रिया अघि बढाइने उनले बताए।

articles.title: पार्टी सदस्यलाई रेडक्रसमा निषेध
articles.summary:
नेपाल रेडक्रस सोसाइटी जिल्ला शाखा भक्तपुरले सक्रिय राजनीतिमा संलग्न व्यक्तिलाई रेडक्रसको सदस्यता तथा नेतृत्वमा स्थान नदिने नीति सार्वजनिक गरेपछि यसको पक्ष–विपक्षमा बहस सुरु भएको छ।

नवनियुक्त जिल्ला सभापति रामेश्वर थापाले पदभार ग्रहण गर्दै रेडक्रसलाई राजनीतिक प्रभावबाट मुक्त राख्ने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरे। उनले अबदेखि विशुद्ध समाजसेवामा समर्पित र कुनै राजनीतिक दलको सदस्यता नलिएका व्यक्तिका लागि सदस्यता खुला गरिने बताए।

‘यसअघि सदस्य बन्न राजनीतिक पहुँच वा दलगत सिफारिस आवश्यक पर्ने अवस्था थियो। अब रेडक्रसमा राजनीति हुन दिइँदैन,’ उनले भने। उनका अनुसार स्वतन्त्र नागरिकका लागि शाखा कार्यालयमै खुला सदस्यता डेस्क सञ्चालन गरिनेछ।

रेडक्रसका जानकारहरूका अनुसार विगतमा सदस्यता वितरण र नेतृत्व चयनमा राजनीतिक प्रभाव देखिने गरेको थियो, जसका कारण संस्थाको निष्पक्षता र विश्वसनीयतामाथि प्रश्न उठ्ने गरेको थियो।

थापाले नेपाल रेडक्रस सोसाइटीको विधान २०२० (अठारौँ संशोधन–२०८२) को दफा ७२(३) अनुसार राजनीतिक दल वा भ्रातृ संगठनका पदाधिकारी तथा राजनीतिक दलबाट राज्यका शासकीय संरचनामा रहेका व्यक्तिहरू रेडक्रसका कुनै पनि तहका समिति, आयोग वा उपसमितिमा सदस्य वा पदाधिकारी बन्न नपाउने व्यवस्था रहेको बताए। दोहोरो भूमिकामा रहेका व्यक्तिलाई रेडक्रसबाट अलग हुन पनि आग्रह गरिएको उनले जानकारी दिए।

रेडक्रसका सात आधारभूत सिद्धान्त—मानवता, निष्पक्षता, तटस्थता, स्वतन्त्रता, स्वेच्छिक सेवा, एकता र विश्वव्यापिता—प्रति प्रतिबद्ध जोसुकै नेपाली नागरिकले निर्धारित प्रक्रिया पूरा गरेर सदस्यता लिन सक्ने व्यवस्था रहेको पनि उनले स्पष्ट पारे।

निर्णयपछि मिश्रित प्रतिक्रिया

भक्तपुर शाखाको घोषणापछि सामाजिक सञ्जालमा भने मिश्रित प्रतिक्रिया देखिएको छ। कतिपयले निर्णयको स्वागत गर्दै रेडक्रसको तटस्थता कायम गर्न आवश्यक कदम भनेका छन् भने केहीले मनोनित पदाधिकारीहरूको राजनीतिक पृष्ठभूमिमाथि प्रश्न उठाएका छन्।

नेपाल रेडक्रस सोसाइटी मध्यपुर थिमि शाखाका पूर्वसभापति बाबुकाजी श्रेष्ठले रेडक्रसमा झन् ठूलो राजनीति सुरु भएको टिप्पणी गरेका छन्। उनले रेडक्रसजस्तो मानवीय संस्थालाई राजनीतिक प्रभावबाट पूर्ण रूपमा मुक्त गर्नुपर्ने आवश्यकता औंल्याएका छन्।

यता मानवीय सेवाका क्षेत्रमा कार्यरत व्यक्तिहरू भने यो व्यवस्थाले रेडक्रसप्रति सर्वसाधारणको विश्वास अझ बलियो हुने अपेक्षा व्यक्त गर्छन्। उनीहरूका अनुसार विपद् व्यवस्थापन, रक्तसञ्चार, उद्धार, राहत र स्वास्थ्य सेवामा सक्रिय रेडक्रसको नेतृत्व राजनीतिक प्रभावभन्दा माथि रहनु आवश्यक छ।

नेपाल रेडक्रस सोसाइटी भक्तपुरमा यसअघिको सम्पूर्ण पदाधिकारी समिति विघटन गरी केन्द्रले रामेश्वर थापाको नेतृत्वमा नयाँ समिति मनोनयन गरेको छ। नवनियुक्त पदाधिकारीहरूको पदस्थापन तथा शपथग्रहण कार्यक्रम बिहीबार भक्तपुरमा सम्पन्न भएको थियो।

articles.title: PM Shah urges calm after deadly unrest
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Thursday appealed for calm after deadly unrest in different districts left three people dead, saying the government would ensure a transparent investigation into the recent violence and hold those responsible accountable.

In a televised address to the nation, Shah said the government was treating the incidents in Sunsari's Dewanganj and parts of Siraha with the utmost seriousness and sensitivity.

Shah said the government had instructed health authorities to ensure prompt treatment for those injured.

He said the home ministry had already formed an investigation committee to examine the incidents and promised that the inquiry would be impartial and transparent. Security forces have been deployed to prevent further violence and restore normalcy, he added.

The prime minister said the home minister had travelled to the affected areas to oversee the security situation, while the National Security Council had reviewed the unrest and taken necessary decisions. He added that an all-party meeting had been convened in Kathmandu and that dialogue was continuing to ease tensions.

Shah urged the public not to spread rumours, misinformation or hate speech through social media or other platforms, asking people to rely only on information released by official government agencies.

Shah also warned that the government would take strict action against anyone attempting to disrupt public order, incite unrest or undermine Nepal's long-standing social harmony.

He appealed to citizens, civil society, religious leaders, political parties and the media to exercise restraint and work together to maintain peace, communal harmony and national unity.

articles.title: Extreme heat threatens Nepal's economy as warming accelerates
articles.summary:
In the scorching mid-June afternoon, as temperatures hovered around 40 degrees Celsius, 67-year-old Gopal Damai was still pulling his rickshaw through the streets of Mahendranagar in far-western Nepal.

For four decades, he has earned his living transporting goods in the three-wheeled cart. But increasingly frequent and intense heatwaves have made that livelihood harder to sustain.

“I only work in the morning and evening. I can't work during the day,” he told Kantipur Daily in May.

“Some days, I don't even earn Rs100. I have to buy vegetables on credit.”

The blistering heat has emptied Mahendranagar's streets. Fewer people venture outdoors during the day, leaving Damai with few customers and even fewer opportunities to earn.

More than 250 kilometres east, in Bardiya's Gulariya Municipality, 37-year-old Puja Bhujuwa faces a similar struggle.

She spends long hours pushing a cart and selling roasted corn near the district land revenue office.

The heat radiating from the asphalt burns her feet, while the 40-degree temperature leaves her with persistent headaches. Despite the oppressive conditions, she must keep roasting corn over a wood fire to support her family.

“Business was good until April,”Bhujuwa told Kantipur in May. “Since June, the heat has intensified, people have stopped coming out during the day, and our sales have dropped sharply.”

The hardships faced by Damai and Bhujuwa illustrate a broader trend.

Extreme heat is no longer confined to Nepal's southern Tarai. Hill towns and cities, including the Kathmandu Valley, are also experiencing steadily rising temperatures, exposing millions of workers to growing health and economic risks.

In Kathmandu, the heat is increasingly taking a toll on informal and daily wage workers who spend long hours outdoors, often without access to shade, cooling facilities or adequate drinking water.

Nepal, long regarded as a cool Himalayan country, is now emerging as one of South Asia's fastest-warming nations, according to the World Bank's 2026 report, A Livable Future: Protecting Jobs and Growth from Extreme Heat in South Asia's Cities.

The report says Nepal has already warmed by 1.26 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels, making it one of the region's fastest-warming countries. Under a medium-emissions scenario, temperatures are projected to rise by another 2.8 degrees Celsius by the end of the century.

The warming will be most pronounced across the Himalayas and foothills, where rising temperatures are expected to alter regional weather patterns, increase humidity and intensify heat across the Indo-Gangetic plains.

Urban centres in Nepal's hills are also warming rapidly. Kathmandu already experiences a pronounced urban heat island effect, with temperatures in the city core reaching up to 4 degrees Celsius higher than surrounding parts of the valley because of dense construction, concrete surfaces and shrinking green spaces.

Although Kathmandu still experiences fewer days of extreme heat than many lowland South Asian cities, the report warns that warming trends indicate even high-altitude cities will increasingly face dangerous heat stress.

Between May 2024 and May 2025, Nepal recorded 89 days with temperatures above the historical 90th percentile, underscoring how quickly extreme heat is becoming the new normal.

According to the World Bank, extreme heat is steadily eroding Nepal's economic productivity by reducing workers' capacity to perform physically demanding jobs, particularly in construction, agriculture and the informal sector. Rising temperatures are also increasing electricity demand, overheating buildings and disrupting transport systems.

Poor households are expected to bear the heaviest burden. Families living in informal settlements often lack reliable electricity, cooling facilities and access to healthcare, making them especially vulnerable to prolonged heatwaves.

The report estimates that more than 700 million people across India, Bangladesh and Nepal already live in areas where outdoor heat stress exceeds safe physiological limits for at least one day every year.

The health burden is also rising rapidly across the region. Across Bangladesh, India, Nepal and Sri Lanka, deaths in which high temperatures were identified as a contributing risk factor nearly doubled between 2000 and 2023—from around 118,000 to approximately 230,000—representing an increase of about 95 percent, or an average annual rise of 4.1 percent.

The report also calls for stronger monitoring of heat-related illnesses and deaths, expanded early warning systems, greener urban planning and the adoption of heat-resilient building standards.

According to the report, embedding heat resilience into urban planning, infrastructure investment and public health systems before temperatures rise further could prevent extreme heat from becoming a long-term constraint on Nepal's economic growth and livability.

The report explains that the human body maintains an internal temperature of about 37 degrees Celsius. Physical activity generates heat, while sweating and the widening of blood vessels near the skin help cool the body. But hotter air, higher humidity and prolonged exposure to direct sunlight or heated surfaces reduce the body's ability to dissipate heat.

When those natural cooling mechanisms fail, people become vulnerable to heat exhaustion, heatstroke and other illnesses that place severe stress on the heart, lungs and kidneys, sometimes resulting in death.

Beyond the health risks, the World Bank warns that extreme heat is already weighing heavily on South Asia's economy.

The equivalent of 31 million full-time jobs are lost annually across the region as workers slow down, stop work early or fall ill. Businesses also suffer as electricity systems, transport networks and buildings struggle to function efficiently under extreme temperatures, reducing productivity, investment and economic output.

According to the report, informal workers' incomes decline by about 40 percent during a heatwave. At the same time, household spending on drinking water, cooling and healthcare rises sharply. Prolonged heat can also force families to borrow money, sell productive assets or pull children out of school to cope with financial stress.

Without adequate adaptation measures, rising temperatures could reduce South Asia's gross domestic product by nearly 7 percent by 2050, the steepest projected decline among developing regions. Shrinking tax revenues coupled with rising public spending on healthcare, energy and damaged infrastructure could create a prolonged fiscal burden for governments.

Dr Prajal Pradhan, associate professor at the Integrated Research on Energy, Environment and Society at the University of Groningen in the Netherlands, said intensifying heatwaves would affect Nepal through both public health and the economy.

“Heatwaves worsen existing illnesses, increase heat-related deaths and reduce labour productivity,” he said.

“As heatwaves become more frequent, demand for cooling will increase, and this requires more electricity. Poor ventilation in buildings also leads to overheating as temperatures rise. Extreme heat can even soften asphalt and disrupt transport systems.”

Pradhan said households living in poorly constructed homes remain highly vulnerable to both cold spells and heatwaves.

“The long-term solution is to ensure decent housing with proper heating and cooling facilities. Expanding green spaces and water bodies in urban areas can also help reduce temperatures and lessen the impact of heatwaves.”

The report said that dense urban areas can remain more than 10 degrees Celsius warmer than surrounding rural areas at night because concrete and asphalt retain heat long after sunset. The lack of nighttime cooling prevents the human body from recovering from daytime heat stress, making prolonged heat exposure even more dangerous.

By 2070, around 520 million people across South Asia are projected to experience at least one month of dangerous heat every year—four times the current number. Much of that exposure will be concentrated in cities, while the Himalayas and their foothills are expected to experience the fastest rate of warming.

The report also warns that the true death toll from extreme heat is likely far higher than official figures indicate because many fatalities are recorded as cardiac or kidney failure rather than heat-related deaths.

Economist Chandra Mani Adhikari said extreme heat is already affecting multiple sectors of Nepal's economy.

“Heatwaves have not only reduced agricultural production but have also significantly affected public health and employment,”he said. “Government and household healthcare spending has risen considerably, while disasters linked to climate change are damaging critical infrastructure.” According to Adhikari, Nepal has failed to adequately strengthen its climate adaptation programmes.

“The current trend suggests Nepal could face growing food insecurity if these problems are not properly analysed and addressed,” he said.

To reduce future losses, the World Bank proposes a broad set of interventions spanning public health, social protection, energy, transport, finance and urban planning.

It recommends investing in early warning systems, strengthening health services, protecting outdoor workers, expanding urban forests and shaded public spaces, and making electricity and transport systems more resilient to extreme heat.

“Heatwaves disrupt every part of city life, so the response must involve the whole of government,” the report says. It also calls for mobilising private investment to expand access to affordable cooling, finance green and climate-resilient buildings, improve cooling systems for industry and healthcare, and develop insurance mechanisms to manage heat-related risks.

Rather than creating entirely new programmes, the report recommends integrating heat resilience into existing initiatives. Employment schemes such as Nepal's National Employment Promotion Programme, national health systems and housing programmes could incorporate heat adaptation measures by updating operational guidelines without requiring major new spending.

The report also highlights the role of frontline community workers. Nepal's Female Community Health Volunteers could help deliver heat advisories and protect pregnant women, children and elderly people through the systems already in place.

As air-conditioning becomes more common, electricity demand is expected to shift increasingly to the evening and night because buildings retain heat after sunset and nighttime temperatures are rising faster than daytime temperatures.

The tourism sector is also expected to face growing risks.

The report recommends retrofitting heritage sites in the Kathmandu Valley—including the Durbar Squares, Pashupatinath, Bauddhanath and Swayambhunath—as well as lowland pilgrimage destinations such as Lumbini and Janakpur with shaded walkways, water features, traditional courtyard ventilation and cool-roof technologies that comply with conservation standards.

According to the report, the Nepal Tourism Board, the Department of Archaeology, UNESCO, the Asian Development Bank and private investors could jointly finance these improvements to protect tourism assets that support an industry worth around $700 million and provide employment for nearly one million people.

The report also recommends strengthening Nepal's electricity network through grid upgrades, distributed renewable energy with battery storage, demand-side management and priority power supply for critical services during periods of extreme heat.

Low-cost interventions such as shaded bus stops, cooler pavements, tree-lined streets and improved pedestrian and cycling infrastructure could also reduce heat exposure, particularly in the Tarai and Kathmandu Valley, according to the report.

articles.title: The entire nation needs to step up to restore harmony in Tarai
articles.summary:
On Thursday evening, Prime Minister Balendra Shah finally addressed the nation after days of unrest across the Tarai-Madhesh triggered by a communal clash in Dewanganj, Sunsari. Since recent events in regions of the southern plains placed the country in a precariously tense situation, it was only right that PM Shah finally took off his sunglasses and peered into the eyes of all citizens, urging them to exercise restraint and maintain societal harmony. The loss of three young lives—Jay Prakash Mehta, Om Prakash Mehta and Ganesh Yadav—and the injuries to scores of citizens and security personnel represent a dreadful tragedy that has heightened a sense of insecurity across the country. With curfews placed in several districts and the spectre of arson and vandalism looming, the fear persists that the situation could spiral beyond control, leading to irreparable damage to the national fabric.

PM Shah’s address to the nation on Thursday was a necessary intervention comprising an appeal for restraint and wisdom. The PM rightly asserted that religion is a “force that unites society and spreads love,” noting that “no religion or culture in the world teaches violence, hatred or division.” By emphasising that the fundamental essence of all religions is compassion, kindness, love and peace, he has sought to steer the public discourse away from the flames of retaliation scourging the Tarai-Madhesh. Such a message is vital in a society that has historically remained liberal towards diverse identities, viewing a mosaic of religions, castes and languages as a defining strength rather than a source of fracture.

Whilst the PM’s commitment to an impartial investigation and his consultation with President Ramchandra Paudel after the broadcast signal mature high-level engagement, the state must also acknowledge its earlier shortcomings. In the initial days of the unrest, security forces struggled with crowd management, and the government’s subsequent reliance on security-centric measures over political strategy was notable. The promotion of harmony now requires more than just the presence of law enforcement. It demands an inclusive strategy of social support and proactive political dialogue.

Furthermore, the inactivity of people’s representatives, particularly those from the Rastriya Swatantra Party who received a significant mandate in these regions, is a matter of concern. True leadership is defined by the ability to manage crises and provide reassurance directly to the electorate. There is an urgent need for representatives at all levels to visit their constituencies, fostering an atmosphere of trust rather than remaining silent in the face of communal tension.

The role of civil society, the media and social media users is equally indispensable. It is imperative to discourage provocative speech and the dissemination of false or unverified information that incites communal disharmony. Instead, the focus must shift towards the promotion of factual, restrained expression that celebrates co-existence.

Ultimately, the responsibility to ‘clear the clouds of unrest’ lies with both the state and the citizenry. Every individual must exercise the wisdom to analyse long-term consequences and reject the malicious interpretations of those seeking to destabilise the nation for ulterior motives. National unity has always been the greatest strength of Nepal during its most challenging periods.

The advancement of security and social harmony within the collective consciousness of a nation must remain the paramount objective of any responsible administration. However, the cultivation of such a climate cannot be achieved through the solitary efforts of the state. It necessitates a sustained, open dialogue and the unwavering support of every stakeholder within the national tapestry. In the words of the Beatles, the entire nation needs to ‘come together, right now’. The government must now act without further delay, prioritising open communication and ensuring that the preservation of social harmony remains the supreme duty of the state. Only through such a concerted effort can the nation transition from this period of unrest towards a future defined by peace and mutual respect.

articles.title: Are we repeating India’s mistakes?
articles.summary:
On Wednesday morning, in an interaction with a closed group of Nepali civil society members, Indian social activist Harsh Mander said that the ‘Citadel of fear’ in India’s socio-political landscape has been dismantled, but the ‘citadel of hate’ still stands. Mander was reflecting on the seismic impact of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests in July. After Chief Justice of India Surya Kant labelled unemployed youth as ‘cockroaches’ on May 15, the CJP reclaimed the slur to forge a satirical, digitally organised group against the system. What began as an online campaign quickly transformed into a mass, leaderless uprising at New Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, driven by fury over leaks in the NEET-UG medical entrance exams and a broader collapse of public trust.

The CJP movement was the inevitable explosion of friction points that have long simmered beneath the surface of the Indian state. For the middle and working class, standardised entrance exams are the primary vehicle for upward social mobility. When these papers leak, as they so often have over the years, years of family savings and student labour are erased. The system had normalised such leaks, with the perpetrators rarely receiving punishment. This was a breach of the meritocratic social contract.

While we regularly see opposition parties and their student wings, both politically motivated, protest paper leaks in India, the CJP protest marked a major departure from the nature of protests, somewhat mimicking September’s Gen Z protests in Nepal. Like Nepal’s movement, the ‘Instagram satyagrahis’ in India bypassed traditional, co-opted political student wings to build a ‘carnival of protest’ that used humour and meme warfare to strip the state of its ability to intimidate them. They forced the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and secured compensation for affected families.

While the current regime in Kathmandu rode to power on the popular anti-establishment rhetoric of September’s protest, Nepal still mirrors Mander’s analogy of citadels, albeit subtly, with a similar layer of digital toxicity that is quietly building a citadel of fear. Across social media platforms, there is an overwhelming, often blind support for the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) and the regime of Prime Minister Balendra Shah. RSP anti-establishment energy has curdled into an aggressive shield that suffocates democratic discourse. Anyone who dares to critique the government faces immediate, seemingly coordinated cyber-harassment.

This digital lynch-mob culture has become so intense that seasoned journalists and public intellectuals have started to self-censor their opinions. The new generation of civil society leaders have been forced to meet behind closed doors, as was the case in Mander’s interaction programme, similar to the underground meetings after Gyanendra’s coup d'état. A portion of these online enforcers can be traced to online groups like Men’s Room Reloaded (MRR)—a Facebook group founded by PM Shah’s chief adviser Kumar Byanjankar—that originated in toxic, pornographic subcultures. This, however, is not an avant-garde practice of the current regime. Previously, the CPN-UML erected an IT cell to cloud critiques against the party and its leaders with opinion-muzzling comments. That such groups are the digital enforcement arms for ruling parties has created a pervasive climate of fear. It was true of UML’s leadership, and it is true now: When citizens are afraid to speak, the vital feedback loops of a healthy democracy are severed.

While the digital citadel of fear rises in Kathmandu, a citadel of hate is simultaneously being constructed along the Tarai belt. The recent communal violence in Sunsari’s Dewanganj, which left one young man dead and 22 others injured, is a chilling warning for the Nepali state. Allegedly triggered by a dispute over loud music during a Bolbam procession, this was not an isolated event. The Armed Police Force (APF) had flagged this growing communal divide three years ago, warning that organised attempts were being made to foment religious and ethnic divisions. The report explicitly urged the government to learn from communal violence elsewhere in South Asia to resolve disputes before they escalated into widespread unrest. However, these warnings were ignored by the political leadership.

If the root causes of the Sunsari incident are not investigated with absolute transparency, Nepal risks normalising the same culture of mob-lynching and communal polarisation that has plagued India for over a decade. The high-handedness of the security response in Sunsari, where police reportedly fired indiscriminately, only deepens public anger.

Meanwhile, silence from PM Shah during this crisis does not help the cause. Except for a social media statement, the PM has been conspicuously absent from the necessary acts of statesmanship. He did not attend the all-party meeting held to address the Sunsari unrest. In a time of national tension, a PM should be the calming voice of the nation, perhaps through a televised address, rather than a distant figure operating through a digital screen.

Furthermore, PM Shah’s relationship with President Ramchandra Paudel has become virtually non-existent, with no substantive consultations taking place in four months. If he continues to govern in isolation, relying on security forces to contain violence rather than political dialogue to prevent it, Nepal will transform into a citadel of hate where the state’s only language is force.

This pattern of administrative arrogance extends to the education sector. The recent Tribhuvan University (TU) leak, where Master of Business Studies (MBS) question papers surfaced in a WhatsApp group of over 1,000 members just five minutes into the exam, is a direct echo of the Indian NEET scandal. While Education Minister Sasmit Pokharel has been praised by his supporters for the swift arrest of the teacher responsible, this is merely a cosmetic PR move if the structural flaws are not addressed. True accountability extends beyond just catching a single ‘Sulav Sir’ to a total restoration of meritocracy in systems like TU and Lok Sewa. As seen in India, when young citizens feel that honest routes to success are rigged, the meritocratic social contract is breached, and their frustration eventually spills onto the streets.

Nepal’s leadership must realise that an anti-establishment origin story does not grant permanent immunity. The same digital tools that built the current regime’s platform can just as easily turn against them if they absorb the ills of the old guard. Governance requires transparent delivery and the courage to engage with criticism rather than social media optics.

When I interviewed Nepali geopolitical analyst Chandra Dev Bhatta for this paper in the aftermath of Nepal’s Gen Z protest, he said that the events in Nepal must have made India restless. While many dismissed Bhatta’s claim as far-fetched, it turned out to be true to an extent. The Indian movement shows that when a government refuses to engage in honest dialogue and chooses intimidation, public anger evolves into an unstoppable, decentralised force. Now, conversely, the events in India have stirred restlessness into the new generation of civil society leaders in Nepal.

Nepal can choose proactive accountability today, or it can continue down a path of enforced silence and digital intimidation until the dam of public patience breaks. The state can either mend the land through trust and integrity now, or wait for the streets to demand a final, unforgiving reckoning.

articles.title: सुनसरी घटनापछि धवलशम्सेरको चिन्ता : शान्ति सुरक्षा कायम गर्न सरकारसँग माग
articles.summary:
राप्रपाका पूर्वमहामन्त्री धवलशम्सेर राणाले तराई क्षेत्रमा बढेको तनावप्रति गम्भीर ध्यानाकर्षण गराएका छन्। उनले सामाजिक सञ्जालमार्फत एक अपिल जारी गर्दै सामाजिक सद्भाव कायम राख्न र शान्ति सुरक्षाको प्रत्याभूति गर्न आग्रह गरेका हुन्।

सुनसरीको देवानगन्ज र कप्तानगन्जबाट सुरु भएको विवाद मधेश प्रदेशका अन्य जिल्लाहरूमा फैलिएपछि तराईको सुरक्षा अवस्था संवेदनशील बनेको छ। झडप, विरोध प्रदर्शन र आगजनीका कारण जनजीवन अस्तव्यस्त हुनुका साथै जनधनको क्षति भएकोप्रति उनले दुःख व्यक्त गरेका छन्।

राणाले भनेका छन्, ‘यस संवेदनशील घडीमा पूर्ण रुपमा जिम्मेवार बनेर शान्ति सुव्यवस्था तत्काल कायम गर्न म नेपाल सरकारको गम्भीर ध्यानाकर्षण गर्दछु। साथै, आम नागरिकको जिउधनको रक्षा गर्दै शान्ति सुरक्षाको पूर्ण प्रत्याभूति दिन सरकारसँग जोडदार माग गर्दछु।’

नेपालको मौलिकता अनेकतामा एकता र विविधताको सम्मान गर्ने सहिष्णु मान्यतामा आधारित रहेको उल्लेख गर्दै उनले सहिष्णुताको विरासत बचाउन सबैको साझा कर्तव्य भएको बताएका छन्।

उनले वार्ता र संवादका माध्यमबाट तनाव अन्त्य गर्न, शान्तिको बाटोबाट समाधान खोज्न तथा धैर्य र संयमता अपनाएर आपसी सद्भावको रक्षा गर्न सम्पूर्ण सरोकारवाला पक्षहरूसँग अनुरोध गरेका छन्।

articles.title: कोटेसाँघुमा चार वर्षपछि पुल बन्दा स्थानीयको सास्ती अन्त्य
articles.summary:
२०७९ साल असोज १९ गतेदेखि २६ गतेसम्म परेको अविरल वर्षासँगै आएको बाढीले जुम्लाको सिंजा गाउँपालिका-३ स्थित कोटेसाँघुमा रहेको मोटरेबल बेलिब्रिज बगाउँदा केवल एउटा पुल मात्र भत्किएको थिएन, गाउँपालिका केन्द्र, वडा नम्बर-२ र नाग्म-गमगढी राजमार्गबीचको दैनिक सम्बन्ध नै टुटेको थियो।

चार वर्षसम्म स्थानीयले जोखिमपूर्ण यात्रा, घुमाउरो बाटो र सेवा लिन अनावश्यक सास्ती भोगे। अहिले त्यही स्थानमा नयाँ मोटरेबल बेलिब्रिज निर्माण सम्पन्न भएसँगै वर्षौंदेखिको समस्या अन्त्य हुने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

२०७९ सालको बाढीले गाउँपालिका केन्द्र नराकोटदेखि नाग्म-गमगढी सडक जोड्ने पुलमा ठूलो क्षति पुर्‍याएको थियो। पुलमात्र होइन, वरपरको भूभागसमेत कटान भएपछि संरचना नदीको बीचमा ठिङ्ग उभिएको जस्तो देखिन्थ्यो। त्यसयता सिंजा-२ का स्थानीयले गाउँपालिका पुग्न आचार्यलिही हुँदै डेढदेखि दुई घण्टासम्म घुमेर जानुपर्ने बाध्यता व्यहोरे।

स्थानीय राजकली वडका अनुसार पुलको अवस्था यति जोखिमपूर्ण थियो कि भारी बोकेर हिँड्न त परै जाओस्, खाली हात वारपार गर्न पनि डर लाग्थ्यो। हिउँदमा अत्यधिक चिसोका कारण नदी तर्न सकिँदैनथ्यो भने बर्खामा भेलबाढीले आवतजावत नै बन्द गरिदिन्थ्यो।

आर्थिक वर्ष २०७८/७९ मा गाउँपालिकाले करिब ५२ लाख रुपैयाँ खर्च गरेर निर्माण गरेको पुल एक वर्ष नबित्दै बाढीले क्षतिग्रस्त बनाएको थियो। त्यसपछि चार वर्षसम्म स्थानीयले यसको प्रत्यक्ष असर भोगे। स्थानीय जनप्रतिनिधिहरूका अनुसार त्यसबेला दीर्घकालीन जोखिमको पर्याप्त अध्ययन नगरी निर्माण गरिएकाले सरकारी लगानी टिकाउ हुन सकेन।

अहिले गाउँपालिकाको आफ्नै बजेट र संघीय सरकारको समपूरक अनुदानबाट करिब साढे ६ करोड रुपैयाँ लागतमा कोटेसाँघु र रनुखाना गरी दुई मोटरेबल पुल निर्माणको योजना अघि बढाइएको छ। तीमध्ये कोटेसाँघुको पुल निर्माण सम्पन्न भइसकेको छ, भने रनुखानाको पुल निर्माण अन्तिम चरणमा पुगेको गाउँपालिकाले जनाएको छ।

गाउँपालिका अध्यक्ष पूर्णप्रसाद धितालका अनुसार २०७९ को विपद्ले बगाएको पुल पुनर्निर्माण स्थानीय सरकारको प्राथमिकतामा परेको थियो। प्रमुख प्रशासकीय अधिकृत टेकबहादुर शाहीले तोकिएको समयअघि नै निर्माण सम्पन्न भएको र छिट्टै पूर्ण सञ्चालनमा आउने बताए।

वडा नम्बर-२ का अध्यक्ष तथा गाउँपालिका प्रवक्ता तीर्थ वडका अनुसार पुल सञ्चालनमा आएपछि गाउँपालिका केन्द्र, वडा नम्बर-२ र नाग्म-गमगढी राजमार्गबीचको दूरी छोटिनेछ। विद्यार्थी, सेवाग्राही, किसान र बिरामीले अब जोखिमपूर्ण यात्रा गर्नुपर्ने बाध्यता हट्नेछ।

कोटेसाँघुको पुल पुनर्निर्माणले चार वर्षअघि बाढीले बगाएको एउटा संरचना मात्र होइन, विकास, सेवा र नागरिकको दैनिक जीवनसँग जोडिएको सम्बन्ध पनि पुनःस्थापित गरेको छ।

पुल निर्माण जिम्मा रिडार्क रवि चक्र जेभी ललितपुरले लिएको थियो। उक्त दुईवटा पुलको ठेक्का एउटै भएको र गत साउनमा ठेक्का आह्वान गरिएको थियो।

articles.title: प्रेस स्वतन्त्रता र श्रमजीवी पत्रकारको अधिकार सुनिश्चित गर्दै ‘टोकियो घोषणा-२०२६’ जारी
articles.summary:
ग्लोबल मिडिया सम्मेलन जापान-२०२६ ले प्रेस स्वतन्त्रताको संरक्षण, श्रमजीवी पत्रकारको अधिकारको कार्यान्वयन, कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता (एआई) को नियमन, तथा प्रवास पत्रकारिताको संस्थागत सुदृढीकरणलाई केन्द्रमा राख्दै ९ बुँदे ‘टोकियो घोषणा-२०२६’ जारी गरेको छ।

नेपाल-जापान कूटनीतिक सम्बन्धको ७०औँ वर्षगाँठको अवसरमा नेपाल पत्रकार महासंघ (एफएनजे) को समन्वय तथा जापान शाखाको आयोजनामा जुलाई २५ मा टोकियोमा आयोजित सम्मेलनमा नेपाल पत्रकार महासंघकी अध्यक्ष निर्मला शर्माको प्रमुख आतिथ्यता रहेको थियो।

कार्यक्रममा महासंघका केन्द्रीय पदाधिकारी, प्रदेश अध्यक्ष, जिल्ला शाखाका प्रतिनिधि, विभिन्न वैदेशिक शाखाका प्रतिनिधि, सञ्चारकर्मी तथा नागरिक समाजका प्रतिनिधिको उल्लेखनीय सहभागिता रहेको थियो।

घोषणापत्रले नेपालमा प्रेस तथा अभिव्यक्ति स्वतन्त्रतामाथि प्रत्यक्ष वा अप्रत्यक्ष रूपमा अंकुश लगाउने कुनै पनि प्रयासप्रति गम्भीर चिन्ता व्यक्त गर्दै संविधान, अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मानवअधिकार सन्धि तथा लोकतान्त्रिक मूल्य-मान्यता अनुरूप प्रेसमैत्री वातावरण सुनिश्चित गर्न सरकारसँग आग्रह गरेको छ। सञ्चारसम्बन्धी कानुन निर्माण वा संशोधन गर्दा सरोकारवालासँग पर्याप्त परामर्श गर्नुपर्ने आवश्यकता पनि औँल्याइएको छ।

सम्मेलनले श्रमजीवी पत्रकार ऐनको पूर्ण कार्यान्वयन, न्यूनतम पारिश्रमिक, सामाजिक सुरक्षा, बिमा, नियुक्तिपत्र तथा अन्य श्रमिक अधिकार सुनिश्चित गर्न सञ्चारगृह र सरकार दुवैलाई जिम्मेवार बन्न आग्रह गरेको छ। नेपाल पत्रकार महासंघले श्रमजीवी पत्रकारका अधिकारका लागि सञ्चालन गरिरहेको आन्दोलनप्रति पनि सम्मेलनले ऐक्यबद्धता जनाएको छ।

सूचना तथा सञ्चार प्रविधिको तीव्र विकाससँगै कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता (एआई) लगायत आधुनिक प्रविधिबाट सिर्जित चुनौतीलाई सम्बोधन गर्न आवश्यक नीति, कानुन र नियामकीय संरचना विकास गर्न सरकार तथा सम्बन्धित निकायलाई सम्मेलनले आग्रह गरेको छ।

घोषणापत्रमा प्रवासमा रहेर नेपाली भाषा, साहित्य, संस्कृति र राष्ट्रिय हितको प्रवर्द्धन गर्दै पत्रकारिता गरिरहेका नेपाली पत्रकारको योगदानको उच्च मूल्यांकन गरिएको छ। महासंघको विधान संशोधन गरी वैदेशिक शाखाका सदस्यलाई चुन्ने र चुनिने अधिकार सुनिश्चित गर्न पहल गर्ने प्रतिबद्धता पनि व्यक्त गरिएको छ।

यस्तै, विश्वभर रहेका वैदेशिक शाखाको प्रभावकारी समन्वयका लागि महासंघको संगठनात्मक पुनर्संरचना आवश्यक रहेको निष्कर्ष निकाल्दै वैदेशिक प्रदेश वा महादेशगत संरचना निर्माण गरी केन्द्रीय समितिमा वैदेशिक शाखाको प्रतिनिधित्व सुनिश्चित गर्न पहल गर्ने निर्णय गरिएको छ।

सम्मेलनले प्रवासमा रहेका नेपाली पत्रकारले आर्जन गरेका ज्ञान, सीप, अनुसन्धान अनुभव र आधुनिक सञ्चार अभ्यासलाई नेपालको पत्रकारिताको विकासमा उपयोग गर्न वैदेशिक शाखालाई ‘ज्ञान हस्तान्तरण’ को प्रभावकारी माध्यमका रूपमा विकास गर्ने प्रतिबद्धता जनाएको छ। साथै गैरआवासीय नेपाली नागरिकलाई राजनीतिक अधिकारबाहेक संविधानले प्रत्याभूत गरेका अन्य संवैधानिक अधिकार व्यवहारमा सहज रूपमा उपभोग गर्न पाउने व्यवस्था सुनिश्चित गर्न सरकारसँग माग गरिएको छ।

घोषणापत्रले वैदेशिक शाखा तथा महासंघसँग सहकार्य गरिरहेका संस्थामा आबद्ध सदस्यको मूल सदस्यता निरन्तर रहने व्यवस्था गर्न तथा जहाँ शाखा स्थापना हुन सकेको छैन, त्यस्ता देशका पत्रकारका लागि डिजिटल माध्यमबाट सदस्यता नवीकरण र व्यवस्थापन गर्ने प्रणाली विकास गर्न आग्रह गरेको छ।

सम्मेलनले विदेशमा कार्यरत नेपाली पत्रकारको योगदानको सम्मानस्वरूप ‘एफएनजे ग्लोबल पत्रकारिता पुरस्कार’ स्थापना गर्ने निर्णय पनि गरेको छ।

घोषणापत्रको अन्त्यमा सम्मेलन सफल बनाउन सहयोग गर्ने जापानस्थित नेपाली दूतावास, गैरआवासीय नेपाली संघ (एनआरएनए) जापान, विभिन्न सामाजिक, सांस्कृतिक तथा व्यावसायिक संस्था, सञ्चारमाध्यम तथा सहभागीहरूप्रति आभार व्यक्त गरिएको छ। साथै सम्मेलन सफलतापूर्वक आयोजना गर्ने नेपाल पत्रकार महासंघ जापान शाखा, अध्यक्ष रविन्द्र श्रेष्ठ (गोर्खाली), सचिव अर्जुन लामिछाने, सम्पूर्ण कार्यसमिति, स्वयंसेवक तथा सहयोगीहरूप्रति विशेष धन्यवाद र सम्मान व्यक्त गरिएको छ।

विश्लेषकहरूका अनुसार टोकियो घोषणा-२०२६ ले प्रवास पत्रकारितालाई केवल सूचना आदानप्रदानको माध्यमका रूपमा नभई नेपाल पत्रकार महासंघको संस्थागत संरचना, नीति निर्माण र पत्रकार अधिकारको बहससँग जोड्ने महत्वपूर्ण दस्तावेजका रूपमा स्थापित गरेको छ। प्रेस स्वतन्त्रता, श्रम अधिकार, डिजिटल पत्रकारिता र प्रवास पत्रकारको संस्थागत सहभागितालाई एकैसाथ समेट्ने यो घोषणा आगामी दिनमा महासंघको नीति तथा विधान संशोधनका लागि मार्गदर्शक बन्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

articles.title: तराईको विषम परिस्थितिप्रति एनआरएनएको चिन्ता : शान्तिपूर्ण समाधान खोज्न आग्रह
articles.summary:
गैरआवासीय नेपाली संघ (एनआरएनए) ले नेपालको सुनसरीको देवानगञ्ज, सिरहा लगायत स्थानमा भएका दुःखद घटना र त्यसपछि केही जिल्लामा हालै विकसित विषम परिस्थितिप्रति गहिरो चिन्ता व्यक्त गरेको छ।

संघका अध्यक्ष डा. हेमराज शर्माले बिहीवार एक विज्ञप्ति जारी गर्दै वर्तमान परिस्थितिलाई यथाशीघ्र सामान्य बनाई नागरिकको जीउधनको सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित गर्न, सामाजिक सद्भाव कायम राख्न तथा समाजमा शान्ति, सुरक्षा र विश्वास पुनःस्थापित गर्न संवाद, सहकार्य, संयम र आपसी समझदारीका माध्यमबाट समस्याको शान्तिपूर्ण समाधान खोज्न नेपाल सरकार, राजनीतिक दल, नागरिक समाज, स्थानीय समुदाय तथा सम्पूर्ण सरोकारवालालाई अनुरोध गरेका छन्।

विज्ञप्तिमा सामाजिक, धार्मिक, जातीय सद्भाव, सहिष्णुता, मेलमिलाप र भ्रातृत्व नेपालको पहिचान भएको उल्लेख गर्दै कुनै पनि प्रकारको हिंसा, द्वेष, घृणा वा विभाजनले राष्ट्र र समाजलाई कमजोर बनाउने बताइएको छ। त्यसैले वर्तमान विषम परिस्थितिलाई यथाशीघ्र सामान्य बनाई नागरिकको जीउधनको सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित गर्न, सामाजिक सद्भाव कायम राख्न तथा समाजमा शान्ति, सुरक्षा र विश्वास पुनःस्थापित गर्न संवाद, सहकार्य, संयम र आपसी समझदारीका माध्यमबाट समस्याको शान्तिपूर्ण समाधान खोज्न सबै सरोकारवालालाई अनुरोध गरिएको छ।

विज्ञप्तिमा यस दुःखद घटनामा परी निधन भएका नागरिकप्रति भावपूर्ण श्रद्धाञ्जली अर्पण गर्दै शोकको कठिन घडीमा शोकसन्तप्त परिवारजन तथा आफन्तहरूप्रति गहिरो समवेदना व्यक्त गरिएको छ।

संघले घाइते सबैको शीघ्र, पूर्ण तथा सफल स्वास्थ्यलाभको हार्दिक कामना गर्दै उनीहरूको प्रभावकारी उपचारका लागि आवश्यक सबै स्वास्थ्य सेवा, उपचार तथा सहयोगको तत्काल व्यवस्था गर्न नेपाल सरकारसँग अनुरोध गरेको छ।

articles.title: सुनसरी घटनापछि धवलशम्सेरको चिन्ता : शान्ति सुरक्षा कायम गर्न सरकारसँग माग
articles.summary:
राप्रपाका पूर्वमहामन्त्री धवलशम्सेर राणाले तराई क्षेत्रमा बढेको तनावप्रति गम्भीर ध्यानाकर्षण गराएका छन्। उनले सामाजिक सञ्जालमार्फत एक अपिल जारी गर्दै सामाजिक सद्भाव कायम राख्न र शान्ति सुरक्षाको प्रत्याभूति गर्न आग्रह गरेका हुन्।

सुनसरीको देवानगन्ज र कप्तानगन्जबाट सुरु भएको विवाद मधेश प्रदेशका अन्य जिल्लाहरूमा फैलिएपछि तराईको सुरक्षा अवस्था संवेदनशील बनेको छ। झडप, विरोध प्रदर्शन र आगजनीका कारण जनजीवन अस्तव्यस्त हुनुका साथै जनधनको क्षति भएकोप्रति उनले दुःख व्यक्त गरेका छन्।

राणाले भनेका छन्, ‘यस संवेदनशील घडीमा पूर्ण रुपमा जिम्मेवार बनेर शान्ति सुव्यवस्था तत्काल कायम गर्न म नेपाल सरकारको गम्भीर ध्यानाकर्षण गर्दछु। साथै, आम नागरिकको जिउधनको रक्षा गर्दै शान्ति सुरक्षाको पूर्ण प्रत्याभूति दिन सरकारसँग जोडदार माग गर्दछु।’

नेपालको मौलिकता अनेकतामा एकता र विविधताको सम्मान गर्ने सहिष्णु मान्यतामा आधारित रहेको उल्लेख गर्दै उनले सहिष्णुताको विरासत बचाउन सबैको साझा कर्तव्य भएको बताएका छन्।
